Protesters across France rally over rising living costs, joining students' grievances
Protesters across France have called for demonstrations against rising living costs, joining high school students demanding better education conditions
PARIS -- Protesters across France called for street demonstrations Saturday against rising living costs, joining high school students' grievances over education conditions after more than three weeks of school blockades.
Saturday’s mobilization follows calls on social media to revive the yellow vest movement, which emerged in 2018 against social injustice. Student groups protesting since mid-September have urged supporters to join.
The CGT, one of France’s major labor unions, also backs the protests, calling for “higher wages and pensions, lower prices and the protection of public services that meet people’s needs.”
President Emmanuel Macron appealed Friday for calm and respect for people and property as officials warned of possible violence.
“There is a constitutional right to protest and to express oneself, and I have always been vigilant and attentive that that right is fully respected,” Macron said Friday in Brussels. “But this right comes with the need to respect. Respect for people, respect for property, and therefore a commitment not to insult or destroy.”
Macron denounced as “unacceptable” the potential presence of people “solely to cause damage and create unrest.”
Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez said hundreds of protest actions and more than 80 marches were expected nationwide, including spontaneous gatherings, street demonstrations and blockades.
In Paris, a march is set to begin in the early afternoon at Republic Plaza, northeast of the city center.
Police banned some other proposed gatherings in central Paris. Many Metro stations were closed Saturday at police request, including those around the Champs-Elysees and near the presidential palace, parliament and government offices.
In recent weeks, France has seen thousands of arrests, hundreds of injuries, and schools set on fire as the new school year descended into nationwide student protests that are influencing the country's presidential election campaign and drawing international attention.
Among protesters, particularly gruesome wounds suffered by some teenagers have been blamed on police riot-control weapons. Nuñez suspended the use of a type of police stun grenade against the young demonstrators after a 15-year-old lost a hand.
On Tuesday, climate and social justice activist Greta Thunberg joined students at a high school in the Paris suburb of Saint-Denis.

Should you limit your FPS in games? Here's when it makes sense
Seeing fewer frames per second sounds counter-intuitive, but there are good reasons to cap your fps.
If you're into PC gaming, there's a good chance you care deeply about frame rates. But even if you own a high-end gaming rig, you should still give serious thought to capping in-game fps. For those looking to boost GPU performance without buying a new one, a system-wide frame rate cap can be a great option. Not only can this help stop screen tearing when combined with V-Sync (vertical synchronization), but a cap can also decrease GPU load.
Is it better to cap your frames or leave them uncapped?
In the majority of games, you should consider capping your frame rate. Setting an fps cap can help you hit and maintain stable performance — provided your hardware is up to the task — while lowering the chance of screen tearing. Capping frame rates can also put less stress on your GPU, leading to reduced fan noise and lower power output in general.
Setting an fps limit makes the most sense if you're using a VRR (Variable Refresh Rate) monitor. That's because a cap helps your favorite games stay inside the effective VRR range, which is generally agreed to start at 48 fps and top out at your display's max refresh rate. By setting a frame rate cap on a VRR screen, you're ensuring the in-game action doesn't hit the refresh rate ceiling, which in turn slightly lowers latency. Paired with V-Sync (much more on this shortly), limiting fps should ensure you never see screen tearing.
If you're wondering what causes screen tearing, this annoying screen issue occurs when your GPU sends a new frame to your monitor/TV while it's still displaying the previous one. This results in different parts of the two frames simultaneously appearing on-screen, which presents as flickering horizontal lines in motion. This looks ugly and can be distracting; it's a game-breaking defect in my book.
I've been capping frame rates for years to get the smoothest, most visually consistent gameplay sessions on my NVIDIA G-Sync compatible monitor. However, I don't usually set a minimum fps level. That's because both G-Sync and AMD's hardware-agnostic FreeSync match a display's refresh rate to a GPU's frame output. Admittedly, I play PC games on a custom RTX 5090 rig, so frame drops are uncommon. But when the action does dip to 110 fps from 120 fps, I can't see or feel the fluctuation.
How to cap frame rates in any PC game
The easiest way to cap a game's frame rate is to use an fps limiter. Many titles have this feature baked into their graphics settings, though they're not always reliable from my experience. A safer bet is to cap your frame rate using your GPU's software.
Those with NVIDIA cards should use either the NVIDIA app or the NVIDIA Control Panel. With the latter, go to Manage 3D Settings > Global Settings > Max Frame Rate, then set your desired fps target. If you have an AMD GPU, you can cap frame rates on a system-wide level with AMD Adrenalin. Simply navigate to Gaming > Radeon Chill, then set your minimum and max fps to the same rate. Another viable option is to use third-party programs, such as Guru3D RTSS RivaTuner.
The rate you should set your output at depends on your display's maximum refresh rate. In most cases, using a combination of V-Sync and a cap of three or four frames below your screen's max refresh rate will stop screen tearing. So if you're on a 60Hz panel, aim for 57 fps. On a 120Hz display, go for 117 fps; 240Hz should be 237 fps and so on.
On VRR displays, capping your frame rate slightly below the max refresh rate can help reduce lag, though not to a significant degree. And if you're concerned about losing a few frames, don't be. You're almost certainly not going to notice the difference between 57 and 60 fps, let alone 237 next to 240. Provided your GPU is powerful enough that it won't dip below the frame rate value you've set, you should get smooth, tear-free gaming experiences on your rig.
The pros and cons of using V-Sync
If you're wondering what V-Sync does to your PC's frames per second, the short answer is that it caps FPS to a number that won't exceed the maximum refresh rate of your display. That means for someone who plays on a 120Hz monitor, your in-game performance can't exceed 120 fps when V-Sync is enabled.
V-Sync synchronizes a game's frame rate to match the refresh rate of a monitor or TV. Before your GPU can push a new frame, V-Sync forces the card to wait until a display's refresh cycle is complete. With 60Hz panels, that introduces a 16.7ms delay. For 120Hz screens, it's 8.33ms, and in the case of ultra-fast 240Hz displays, just 4.17ms.
The obvious plus with V-Sync is that it all but eliminates the chance of screen tearing. That's great, since screen tearing is an absolute immersion-breaker. Yet there's a fairly sizable downside to enabling V-Sync. By forcing the GPU to wait until individual refresh rate cycles are complete before it can generate fresh frames, unavoidable input lag is added.
The amount of latency V-Sync adds often varies by game. A rule of thumb is to expect one additional refresh cycle of lag. So with a 120Hz monitor, that's once again 8.33ms. Of course, if your GPU can't render frames fast enough, queued frames will build up, increasing latency even further.
In my experience, V-Sync has never added noticeable lag. For hardcore shooter fans using Team Green GPUs who crave the smoothest performance in order to pull off consistent headshots, it's worth playing around with NVIDIA V-Sync Fast. Found in the NVIDIA Control Panel under Manage 3D settings, this feature aims to reduce standard V-Sync lag while also providing a lower-tear experience.
Fast V-Sync lets the GPU keep rendering frames rather than make it wait for a refresh cycle to complete, so it doesn't cap FPS like garden variety V-Sync. I've had decently slick results with Fast V-Sync in games where my frame rate is normally well over my monitor's refresh rate; if you're often in this situation, it's another option to eliminate tearing, though it doesn't work in all games.

Deaths confirmed after 'serious incident' causes fire at Canadian military base
In short:
Canadian Defense Minister David McGuinty says people have been killed and injured in a serious incident that resulted in a fire on a military base in Alberta.
The blaze started at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright at around 4pm on Saturday, local time.
What's next?
Authorities are still working to determine what happened and expect to provide further information soon.
People have been killed and injured in an incident at a military base in Alberta that caused a major fire, according to Canada's defence minister, while the media is reporting that large numbers were being transported to hospitals.
Fire crews scrambled late into the night as fierce winds whipped flames beyond Canadian Forces Base (CFB) Wainwright and into the surrounding rural area.
It was not immediately clear how many people were killed or injured, but a doctor at a hospital in the city of Edmonton, 180km north-west, told Canada's national broadcaster that patients were being brought to hospitals across the city as healthcare facilities around the base became "completely overwhelmed" by the number of people needing treatment.
"This number of patients would overwhelm the city of Edmonton," Warren Thirsk, an emergency department physician at the Royal Alexandra Hospital, told CBC News.
"It is more patients than any of us want to count right now. It's a disaster. It's a one in every 15- to 25-year disaster."
The town of Wainwright, near the base, has about 7,000 residents.
Defense Minister David McGuinty said the Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP) were involved in investigating the incident and described the situation as "very, very active and delicate."
He said authorities were still working to determine what happened and expected to provide further information soon.
The RCMP said officers were called shortly after 4pm on Saturday following reports of a fire in a training area at the base.
Firefighters faced a volatile situation.
Large areas of the province were hit during the day by a windstorm with gusts of up to 100 kilometres an hour.
The wind toppled some trees and sent signs flying and garbage cans rolling down streets.
By 11pm, the Municipal District of Wainwright said on social media the fire was being held, and that property and critical infrastructure were protected.
There was no evacuation order for residents.
Mr McGuinty, speaking to reporters in Ottawa, confirmed the casualties but had no other details to share.
"I cannot recall such an incident in my short time for sure as a minister, but I cannot recall an incident like this in recent memory," Mr McGuinty said.
"We will have more to say in the coming hours and days."
He said armed forces members were at the scene and that RCMP were also involved.
"This is an active and delicate situation and soon to be an active and delicate investigation,"
he said
Saskatchewan Premier Scott Moe said his province was sending assistance to Alberta but did not specify what resources were being deployed.
"Our thoughts are with all the brave women and men affected," Prime Minister Mark Carney said earlier in a social media post.
Alberta Premier Danielle Smith described the fire as "significant and tragic" and said it was affecting many military personnel.
CFB Wainwright is one of Canada's busiest military training bases, where soldiers prepare for combat operations.
It is home to the Canadian Manoeuvre Training Centre, which conducts realistic battlefield exercises, and the 3rd Canadian Division Training Centre, which provides military training.
Canadian Conservative opposition leader Pierre Poilievre said he had spoken with Mr Carney and the defence minister to offer support to those affected by the fire.
"Pray for Wainwright, everyone," Mr Poilievre said.
He urged people in the area to follow emergency instructions and keep roads clear for first responders.
The fire also disrupted advance voting ahead of Monday's referendum on whether Alberta should begin a process that could lead to independence from Canada.
Elections Alberta said two polling locations, in Lloydminster and Vermilion, closed early on Saturday and the ballots were transported securely.

Neverwinter Nights was made by the studio that produced seminal RPGs Baldur’s Gate, Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic, Mass Effect, and Dragon Age. It sold well and was critically acclaimed at launch. Yet, somehow, it has not been canonized in most gamers’ minds over the decades the same way the games that came before and after it were.
Nonetheless, more than two decades later, it still has a tight-knit and surprisingly active community that none of those other games can rival. I think that’s partly because it was a completely different beast.
BioWare is known for making multi-character, story-driven role-playing games that focused primarily on single-player story campaigns, though some supported co-op play in those campaigns. With Neverwinter Nights, BioWare instead made a game that was as focused on a modding toolset for content creation as it was on giving players a pre-packaged story, and that emphasized multiplayer at least as much as solo play.
Today you would expect this to be a calculated attempt to bring more long-term, always-on, multiplayer-as-a-service to an RPG franchise that has mostly appealed to solo players. You might imagine it would be about selling cosmetics, a subscription, or a battle pass, or maybe you would think it was about nabbing appealing engagement numbers.
But it’s clear from playing it today that Neverwinter Nights wasn’t primarily made for those reasons. Instead, it came from a passion for tabletop role-playing and a desire to get closer to that in video game form than ever before.
Yes, the BioWare team noted in some interviews that they saw this as a trial run for exploring the idea of making a massively multiplayer game (MMO)—something that, in the year 2000, was seen by many as the hot new business opportunity in gaming, and which was in many ways the precursor to the games-as-a-service we see today. They then indicated they realized that an MMO was harder to make than they had assumed and abandoned that ambition well before Neverwinter Nights shipped.
Neverwinter Nights is not exactly an MMO. Instead, it’s designed for small communities of people to inhabit and create with, and it features a powerful toolset for virtual dungeon masters to use to subject regular players to challenges in an improvisational way on a live server.
“We always envisioned it as a table with four legs—the single player, the multiplayer, the DMing tools and the toolset (the module making tools),” BioWare’s Ray Muzyka told IGN around the time the game was released. “They all appeal to different groups, and we’ve tried to make them all equivalently high quality.”
Over the past month, I’ve been replaying Neverwinter Nights‘ main story campaign, The Wailing Death, as a solo player, for the first time in 20 years. The nostalgia has been strong in this replay, but I have also found that BioWare didn’t quite nail “equivalently high quality” for all the pillars. Still, it doesn’t matter, because as we’ll see when we check in with the game’s community, the campaign is not the point.
“The single player experience has to be as good as anything we’ve ever done in [Baldur’s Gate], [Baldur’s Gate 2], or Throne of Bhaal and hopefully better,” Muzyka told IGN. “Our goal here at BioWare is that each game we do has to be better than the previous one.”
If single-player is one of the legs, it might be fair to call Neverwinter Nights‘ table a little wobbly. It still stands, but you know how irritating it can be.
For example, Neverwinter Nights leaves behind Baldur’s Gate or Icewind Dale‘s party-based systems, and instead has the player controlling just one character directly. It makes sense for a multiplayer game, but doesn’t work as well for a single-player experience in this case—at least with the Dungeons & Dragons rules of the time.
I chose to play a monk, a martial arts specialist, simply because I’ve always been drawn to that particular fantasy identity, and because I’d never played one in a D&D game. I regretted that decision after a while.
For many of the character levels covered in The Wailing Death, the monk basically just picks between two fighting modes: one that misses more but attacks more frequently, and one that’s just normal. That, along with some intense restrictions on which weapons or armor can be used while keeping all their benefits, and a couple of knockdown and stun attacks that often don’t work, make up the whole kit for many hours of playtime, particularly in the first act. (It does get better later on, though.)
The original campaign is fun and nostalgic, but it’s arguably not BioWare’s best.
The original campaign is fun and nostalgic, but it’s arguably not BioWare’s best.
Credit:
GOG
A kit like this makes sense in a pen-and-paper RPG with a live dungeon master (DM), because the player and DM can work together to invent creative expressions of their abilities, and it works in a party in a video game because it’s just one of multiple complementary characters with a wide range of skills and spells.
But for a game that is about 80 percent battling enemies without controlling any other characters, it gets monotonous quickly. There aren’t as many meaningful character builds, gearing, or tactical choices as you’re used to in some other RPGs until quite a ways into the campaign. Often, you just run in and watch the dice roll until either you die or the enemy dies, while sometimes drinking potions.
This problem is less severe with some other classes, but the tension is usually there to some degree.
Whereas Baldur’s Gate 2, for example, had a partial authored background for your character that then played into the narrative, Neverwinter Nights leaves you as an Elder Scrolls-like blank slate. I normally love that! It’s good for role-playing with friends, because you can make up your own character completely. But it means the story can’t be character-driven, and the gameplay doesn’t provide enough flexibility or freedom in return.
Still, I enjoyed my experience with the campaign when I replayed it recently, even if it couldn’t match Baldur’s Gate 2, Knights of the Old Republic, Mass Effect, or other BioWare classics for me personally. While the story wasn’t anything special by BioWare’s standards, there was something genuinely cozy to me about the genericness of the narrative. It took me back to an earlier time in CRPGs, before things got quite so precious. “This is just like D&D!” was still enough to sell it on its own. Maybe it’s just nostalgia, though.
Since most people played the game solo, and it was a relatively small portion of the player base that dove deep into the construction kit or DM tools, I think this is the main reason Neverwinter Nights has not achieved the same pantheon status as other BioWare titles that came before and after it.
But for those lucky few who were invested in those other table legs, it actually was quite special—and amazingly, it remains so today.
The persistent worlds of Neverwinter Nights
“The main thing I would shout from the rooftops if I could, is that firing up Neverwinter Nights and launching its original campaign… does not do justice to what Neverwinter Nights has become since,” a longtime player named Daniel Morris told me. He goes by Irongron in the community, and he runs Arelith, which is both one of the OG persistent multiplayer servers and one of the most popular servers today. Morris is also working on a visual overhaul of the original campaign; he hopes to release it next year.
Arelith hit its peak player count “a little less than two years ago,” as Morris tells it—not way back when the game was new. “Our community is the heart of Arelith, it’s not just our audience, but where we find our DMs and developers,” he said.
Arelith is a fountain of creativity; for example, this is original artwork commissioned for the game’s loading screens from artist Matheus Graef.

I spent many evenings in my younger days playing multi-user dungeons (MUDs), the text-based online role-playing games that preceded MMOs like EverQuest or World of Warcraft. While there were big MUDs, many were small communities of just one or two dozen people, and often, those same people were the ones actually making the game’s content. For example, I was a room builder for one MUD; I wrote the descriptions for places in the MUD’s world and decided which monsters, NPCs, or items inhabited those places.
Neverwinter Nights‘ multiplayer platform and community—both as it was back in the 2000s and as it is today—reminds me of those MUD days. There’s an ownership of that shared world that is entirely lost in the MMO days, perhaps more akin to a modern, small Minecraft server than an MMO with thousands of users.
That seems to be part of the appeal for a player I spoke with who goes by the name NelaK in the community, and who has, among other things, taken over maintenance and moderation of the Neverwinter Vault, the community’s de facto hub for two decades. The website hosts news, patches, assets, mods, a forum, a wiki, and an associated Discord server.
“It’s not an MMO, and that’s a good thing in my opinion. The communities are smaller, which means your roleplay and your actions matter and can affect the world,” said NelaK. “The world itself can be tailored around what the players want. That’s a unique thing that you can’t get from an MMO or from smaller-scale multiplayer games. It sits in a sweet spot where you can have enough players that it feels like a proper community and a world you can engage with while you can still matter.”
Baldur’s Gate and Icewind Dale did have multiplayer, where each player could control one or more characters directly. As noted, Neverwinter Nights limits each player to one character, but it adds a new role: a dungeon master, who can spawn enemies, occupy and act as NPCs, and more, to aid in group storytelling, similar to a pen-and-paper game.
“While Arelith is essentially a mini MMO, many of the other servers pride themselves in running highly curated, beautifully crafted campaign worlds much closer to tabletop role-playing game emulator that Neverwinter Nights was first intended as,” Morris told me. He called Neverwinter Nights “a direct translation of the tabletop role-playing game experience into the digital sphere.”
It’s as much a construction kit as it is a game
The game’s modding kit and easy-to-use scripting tools let players build scenarios relatively quickly. It essentially let players build a little RPG world, run it, and inhabit it. It was a bustling scene back then, and there’s still a community doing this today. The combination of the relative simplicity of the graphics and the elegance of the tools make this toolset an unusually excellent balance between flexible, powerful, and easy to learn.
“The tile-based areas are basic and limiting in some respects, but they do mean that building areas is quick and easy,” explained NelaK. “It’s much more approachable than a lot of other platforms.”
For NelaK and some other members of the game’s community today, the game’s tools aren’t just the remaining appeal—they’re the main appeal.
“I’ve been playing Neverwinter Nights since launch day. I remember one of my friends dragging me along to the store because they really wanted the game and I went just to keep them company,” he remembered. “I ended up buying it, and I’ve been hooked ever since, but to this day, I’ve still never played through the original campaigns… and yet I’ve played Neverwinter Nights or spent time building or working on something Neverwinter Nights-related most days since.”
I toyed around with the tools quite a bit back in the day. I remember re-creating a big chunk of the world of my favorite MMO at the time, Meridian 59, with the intent to make a story-driven, single-player campaign for that game; Meridian 59 had very little narrative as it was.
I also remember that Neverwinter Nights was for many years a common way for would-be narrative designers to make a portfolio piece for applying for jobs within the games industry. When I was in college, a close friend of mine (Brian “Psychochild” Green, who at the time co-ran Meridian 59, and sadly has since passed) offered to show my Neverwinter Nights modules to some friends of his at BioWare if I wanted to interview for a job there to write for their next game, which, based on timing, probably would have been Mass Effect. I declined in order to focus on other priorities I had at the time, for better or worse.
Similarly, many (though certainly not all) people in the community have professional backgrounds closely related to, or at least adjacent to, game development.
“Neverwinter Nights provides a unique intersection of where I can apply my technical and professional skills along with my interest in video games and do it for something that doesn’t feel like work,” said NelaK. Morris specifically noted that several members of the Arileth team work or have worked in the games industry or software development.
This is the game’s legacy, not the story campaigns that shipped with the game. And that explains the game’s relative obscurity today: that’s a more niche appeal than a really good, story-driven, single-player RPG. But for the people who are into it, there’s nothing else that quite compares.
Returning to Neverwinter Nights today
I don’t imagine most people still regularly see references to Neverwinter Nights, but I sometimes do. For the past couple of years, I’ve enjoyed the dark fantasy trend on TikTok. These are short, vertical videos set to a particular kind of 1980s fantasy-type medieval synth music, depicting imagery from what feels like a long-lost, strangely nostalgic subgenre of fantasy media that is more implied in our memories’ liminal space between real fantasy movies and books of the ’80s and early ’90s than it is something that actually specifically existed.
It turns out Neverwinter Nights‘ assets fit that milieu quite well, so I sometimes saw videos of people creating online Neverwinter Nights servers meant to capture that vibe. It’s niche as hell, but it’s there. The TikTok videos from one of the game’s servers were actually how I got inspired to try the game again.
“Over the last year there’s been a bit of a resurgence, with new servers going live, and others going viral,” Morris told me. Some player-run servers “have had hundreds of thousands interacting with their TikTok videos.”
He added that his own community’s Discord server has 5,000 members, and that’s just one part of the game’s wider audience.
If you want to get back into the game or try it for the first time, you can buy the Enhanced Edition on GOG and other storefronts; a front-page poll on the Neverwinter Vault indicates that about 65 percent of the community primarily uses that version, as compared to previous releases or the sequel, Neverwinter Nights 2.
If you want to try the single-player, the Enhanced Edition comes with a plethora of officially sanctioned campaigns of varying quality—not just The Wailing Death.
But let’s say you, like some members of the game’s current community, are more interested in multiplayer than single-player. A good place to start is the Neverwinter Vault. Additionally, Enhanced Edition developer Beamdog hosts a list of active community servers you can join.
As I write this, a few hundred people are playing across a couple dozen servers, which is impressive. I love to see old games like this keep the community going. It’s especially important for Neverwinter Nights, because more than any other BioWare game or even most other RPGs in general, this game is its community.

India’s youth-led Cockroach movement kicked off more nationwide protests on Friday as thousands of people gathered in Mumbai, amid mounting concerns that millions of citizens are being unfairly stripped of their vote.
The movement, which calls itself the Cockroach Janta party (CJP) and has massive support among the country’s gen Zs, returned to the streets to demand the resignation of the chief election commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar.
Kumar has become a highly contentious figure after a report in the Indian Express newspaper alleged irregularities and internal concerns about a process to revise and “purify” India’s electoral register, called the Special Intensive Revision (SIR).
SIR, which was overseen by Kumar, has resulted in tens of millions of people being deleted from the electoral register. Large numbers are challenging their removal.
Opposition politicians and civil society groups have alleged SIR is part of a widespread manipulation of India’s electoral system to benefit the ruling Bharatiya Janata party (BJP).
The CJP began as online satire but grew into a powerful manifestation of youth power and an unexpected challenge to the Narendra Modi government. There were protests for weeks in the heart of Delhi and the education minister was eventually pressured into resigning in July. In the aftermath, the group declared it would remain active as a “pressure group” to hold the government to account on issues of education and democracy.
Last week, after the revelations about the election commission, the CJP’s founder, Abhijeet Dipke, announced that if Kumar did not resign over the controversy, the “Cockroaches” would resume their agitation until he stepped down. Dipke said the Mumbai protest would kick off a nationwide movement, with more protests planned in Delhi, Goa, Kolkata and Bengaluru.
The authorities denied permission for the group to hold their protest at Mumbai’s Shivaji park but Dipke had vowed to go ahead regardless. “We are fighting against those in power,” he said, at a press conference. “We all remember Mahatma Gandhi, who fought against the Britishers. Did the British ever permit him to agitate?”
Hundreds of people assembled in Mumbai on Friday afternoon, amid a heavy police presence, including many young people who said they were there to fight for India’s democracy.
“Voting is the most basic right of any citizen, but because of the actions of Kumar and the election commission, that right is under attack,” said Deesha, 22, a student activist. “So many millions of people have lost their votes and aren’t even recognised as citizens of India any more. This attack on our democracy must stop. The first important step is to get Gyanesh Kumar to resign, and then SIR must be reversed.”
Janvi Upadhyay, 18, said that the Cockroach movement had awoken the young people of India “and if they think they can just come and take away votes and cheat the elections, we will show them just how wrong they are”.
“We already forced the education minister to resign. Gyanesh Kumar should be very worried right now because he is definitely next,” she said.
The election commission has denied wrongdoing in the SIR but in a move that appeared aimed at easing tensions, officials were directed to expedite the process to register newly eligible voters and those who claimed to have been wrongly omitted from electoral rolls.
Anger at Kumar and the election commission also erupted in Delhi on Friday, even as the police took draconian measures to try and stop people from protesting. Thousands of police were deployed to the Jantar Mantar protest site in Delhi – which was the epicentre of the last Cockroach agitation in July – a dozen metro stations in the surrounding area were closed and an internet shutdown was imposed.
Hundreds of those who turned out to Jantar Mantar were immediately forced into police buses. The mass detentions of at least 700 people, including civil society leaders and opposition politicians, prompted outrage, with protesters leaning out of the bus windows to accuse police officers of depriving them of their fundamental democratic rights.
Opposition parties said they would also start a nationwide protest movement to demand Kumar’s resignation. All opposition lawmakers plan to march to the election commission office in Delhi next week.

The Central Reserve Police Force (CRPF), India's largest paramilitary force, is reportedly considering reintroducing the military ranks of lance naik and naik, roughly 30 years after they were abolished, officials told PTI on Saturday.
The move aims to address delayed promotions and accommodate Agniveers leaving the Army. The proposal would restore the two ranks abolished in 1997, creating additional promotion opportunities for constables before they become head constables.
The CRPF has around 3.25 lakh personnel, but its constables wait an average of 22–25 years for their first promotion, according to the report. Officials said spending so many years in a single rank has led to discontent among personnel.
Bringing back the lance naik and naik ranks would give constables two opportunities for promotion before reaching the head constable rank. The move could help address these grievances and boost morale in India’s largest paramilitary force.
Officials said the proposal also aims to attract Agniveers leaving the Army. Their first batch is expected to finish its service later this year and will be eligible to join the Central Armed Police Forces (CAPFs), including the CRPF. Under the Centre's Agnipath scheme, Agniveers are recruited into the three armed services for four-year terms.
The CRPF and the Border Security Force (BSF) once included lance naik and naik in their rank structures, following the model of the Army’s infantry battalions. Under this hierarchy, a jawan joining as a constable would be promoted to lance naik after five years of service, naik after 10 years, and head constable after 20 years.
While both ranks remain in use in the Army, an order from the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) abolished them in the CRPF nearly three decades ago, merging them with the ranks of constable and head constable.
If approved and implemented, the proposal would restore intermediate steps between constable and head constable, allowing personnel more opportunities to advance within the constabulary.
CAPFs currently allow constables to wear senior constable insignia corresponding to the lance naik rank under an ad hoc system. Senior constable, however, is not a sanctioned rank, and no similar provision exists for naik.
It remains unclear whether restoring the ranks would guarantee promotions within a fixed period. Ranbir Singh, secretary general of the Ex-Paramilitary Personnel Association, said the proposal would help personnel only if promotions followed a set timeline; without that, the exercise would serve little purpose.
A senior CRPF commandant said the decision to reintroduce the two Army ranks should "not just be a cosmetic move and should ensure that the discipline of the battalion is maintained".
The commandant further noted that a battalion of over 1,000 men and women currently has over 20 subordinate officers. Any change to the rank structure, according to the commandant, should account for the unit’s regimentation and operational efficiency.
CRPF headquarters has directed hundreds of its field formations across the country to gather personnel's feedback on the proposal within two days through stakeholder meetings, or 'Sainik Sammelans', officials said. The proposal remains under consideration.

Psst—I’m going to let you in on a little secret as a smart-home editor. Even though I now own the much-lauded Ecobee Premium ($260) smart thermostat, I had an Ecobee3 Lite for eight years, and I loved it just as much. It's everything you need a smart thermostat to be, without weird add-ons you'll never actually use, like occupancy detection and a built-in speaker for podcast streaming. (Unless you regularly listen to Uncanny Valley on your thermostat, in which case, you do you.)
The Ecobee3 Lite has a touchscreen and app control and is compatible with Ecobee sensors if you want to split the temperature difference across floors in your home. However, many people simply want to be able to turn their thermostat on and off from their phone and have the ability to set schedules. For this, the Lite has you covered.
Though it's been formally rebranded as the Essential and now runs $140, the OG Lite is still available refurbished straight from Ecobee. During the brand's fall sale, it's just $120 with free shipping—and it comes with the same three-year warranty as a new model.
If you've been wanting to upgrade your thermostat but missed Prime Day and don't want to wait until Black Friday, you may want to take a peek at this sale, which ends Wednesday, October 21.
Refurbished versions of the Enhanced ($170) and Premium ($220) thermostat models are available as well, plus packages that include Ecobee security accessories. I have tried most of the brand's add-ons and find Ecobee to be a bit buggy as a security and smart-home ecosystem (not the best, but also not the worst); however, I do heartily recommend the smart thermostat alone.
If you already have an Ecobee thermostat, you can also score a set of not-refurbished security sensors for $50, or the Ecobee video doorbell for $130, which lets you see and speak to visitors through your phone—or thermostat.

Summer is officially over, along with its allotment of free sunlight. You might be sad about this, but your indoor plants might be even sadder. A good LED grow light can replicate sunlight with full-spectrum light and day/night cycles, keeping plants lush and thriving even in a dark, windowless corner or basement.
I have no fewer than 40 houseplants in my home at any given time, as well as a fair number of grow lights, and what I've found to be important for a general consumer (i.e., someone not doing that kind of indoor grow) isn't necessarily certain colored light wavelengths but whether a grow light is easy to live with in your house.
Many grow lights are more or less going to serve the same purpose, so what you really need to know is this: Is the light so bright that it's disruptive? Does it require complicated installation? Is it easy for kids or pets to knock over? The grow lights recommended below are ones that WIRED staffers have lived with for months, if not years, and have found them both effective and easy to integrate into our lives.
Also be sure to check out our guides to the Best Indoor Gardening Systems, Best Gifts for Plant Lovers, and Best Kitchen Composters.
Featured Lights
What Is PPFD?
Photosynthetic photon flux Ddensity, or PPFD, expressed in micromoles per square meter per second (μmol/m²/s), is a measurement of how much light reaches your plant that's usable for photosynthesis. In general, the higher the plant's energy needs, such as producing a flower or a fruit, the higher the PPFD number you want. Though different lights have different height requirements given the plants they're made for, for standardization purposes, I measured the PPFD of each grow light at 18 inches with the Photone app and a light diffuser. Keep in mind these measurements are general and approximate.
How I Test Grow Lights
Some of these grow lights I bought myself, with my own money, before I even began working at WIRED. Others were owned by staffers and recommended to me. I also have press samples from other guides I worked on, which I liked so much I ended up keeping around.
For the traditional grow lights, I tested them at home under normal-life conditions. I put them where they'd fit, tested their timers, and noted whether or not they were dimmable. I also measured each light's PPFD (see above) and noted whether certain lights could be daisy-chained for more extensive coverage.

Best Grow Light for Small Plants and Seedlings
There are a lot of options out there for starting seeds and helping houseplants along in the winter, and many of them are bulky, fussy, or require elaborate hanging setups. This simple, 15-inch-long light from Vego sticks to its 3M adhesive mount with a magnet, so it's easy to take on and off and use with existing racks or, as I do, under a kitchen cabinet. Up to four Vego lights can be daisy-chained together, and the five preprogrammed modes (Seeds, Leafy, Fruits, Herbs, Microgreens) have varying intensities and automatic built-in off periods to simulate nighttime. I have not found this light especially disruptive, especially since it's easy to turn on and off with the button on the back.
WIRED commerce SEO director Stewart Savin used these lights to start her garden earlier this year and had 138 successful germinations across 144 seedling cells. ("The vast majority of those plants went on to have long lives in my garden after I hardened them off," she says.) Note that because this light can only go beneath a rack, shelf, or cabinet, it’s not inherently adjustable, and therefore is best for small plants (like seedlings) that aren’t going to grow especially tall.

A Mexican judge has sentenced three men to 158 years and nine months in prison each for the murder of two Australian brothers and their American friend during a 2024 surf trip to the state of Baja California.
The defendants were declared guilty a week ago of homicide, aggravated robbery, robbery with violence and vehicle theft with violence, crimes committed against Australian brothers Jake and Callum Robinson, and their American friend Carter Rhoad.
Rhoad and the Robinsons were shot dead in a suspected robbery while travelling through Mexico.
They were camping in a remote beachside area near the city of Ensenada when they were attacked on 27 April 2024.
Their bodies were found days later in a clifftop well with gunshot wounds to the heads.
Jesus Gerardo – known as “El Kekas” – was accused of leading the attack. His surname has not been disclosed for legal reasons.
Two other defendants, Irineo Francisco and Angel Jesus, were also found guilty and have been sentenced.
The families of the victims followed the sentencing hearing via video link.
Prosecutors had requested damages of more than $100,000 but the judge ruled against it and said any compensation would have to be pursued through civil proceedings.
The brothers’ parents, Martin and Debra Robinson, travelled from Australia to the port city of Ensenada for the trial, which began on 7 September.
They have established a foundation in their sons’ names to carry on their legacy.
The Callum and Jake Robinson Foundation aims to “help people live bigger, shine brighter and love harder in their honour”.
Callum, the older of the two brothers, moved to the US as a professional lacrosse player and has been remembered for his loving nature and passion for the environment, having been involved in coastal cleanups.
Jake, a doctor, was set to take up a position at Geelong hospital after returning to Australia.
He has been remembered for his academic success, his passion for sport, particularly cricket and surfing, and his compassion.
Baja California is one of Mexico’s most violent states, plagued by organised crime and drug trafficking, although cartel activity does not usually affect tourists. Other foreign visitors have, however, been targeted in criminal attacks on Mexico’s Pacific coast.
Two Australian surfers, Dean Lucas and Adam Coleman, were killed in 2015 while travelling through the north-western state of Sinaloa. Their bodies were later burned.

Oregon teacher fought school attacker before armed dad shot suspect 'multiple times'
- Published
An Oregon teacher threw her mobile phone before she tackled and tried to wrestle away a shotgun from the arms of a teen suspect who opened fire on a special educational needs class.
As she tussled with him on the floor of the class - where three children and a teacher were killed - a bystander ran inside. Armed with a .40-caliber pistol, he opened fire and killed the teen.
The bystander, a dad of two girls at the school, had been driving past Silver Rail Elementary in Bend when he saw the suspect firing in the car park then shooting through a window to enter.
The details of the Thursday attack were confirmed by police, who said the 16-year-old suspect was a prior student at the school.
Police say the suspect was armed with about 44 more rounds of shotgun ammunition when he was stopped. He fired as many as 15 rounds in the class.
"To the people who showed courage in the face of such violence, and intervened to prevent this tragedy from being any worse, we owe you a debt of gratitude," Bend Police Chief Mike Krantz said on Friday.
Police offered more information on the attack at at a news conference on Friday, where they identified two of the four victims. They include five-year-old Rhoam Summer and 25-year-old teacher Meghan Lambert.
The families of the two other students who were killed, an eight-year-old and 11-year-old, did not wish to have them publicly identified yet, police said.
Two others were injured in the attack. Another teacher, a 54-year-old, was still being treated at hospital, and a seven-year-old student, who was in serious but stable condition.
Krantz said the heroic actions of both the teacher and the father who ran inside the school saved lives.
He said the teacher who wrestled with the gunman was not hurt but "almost certainly helped prevent more bloodshed".
He identified the suspect as 16-year-old Griffin J. John II, who previously attended the school and was a special educational needs student there.
A search warrant has been executed at the suspect's home and a search is ongoing, the police chief said.
Police believe the suspect travelled to the elementary school on foot, but police are still investigating his exact movements and how he acquired the gun. A motive is also not clear.
Officials did not confirm the name of the father who intervened and fatally shot the suspect.
But Kaylub Giamanco's family has identified him to US media as the person who sprang into action.
The 36-year-old carpenter had just finished lunch and was on his way home when he passed the school, his brother told NBC News. He saw the suspect open fire on a vehicle outside the school then shoot through a window and go inside.
Police said he had a legally concealed .40 caliber in his vehicle and his brother said he grabbed the pistol "and decided to go in after" the suspect. Police say he fired at the suspect "multiple times", killing him.
In a statement to the BBC's partner CBS News, Giamanco's family said he is a "lifelong resident of Bend" and that he "is not seeking recognition".
The family said Giamanco wants to express his "gratitude to the first responders, school personnel, and community for the outpouring of love and support". He and his family "respectfully ask for privacy".
US President Donald Trump praised the bystander's actions on Friday, calling him a "great hero".
Addressing reporters at the White House before departing for Georgia, Trump said the situation could have been "much worse" with no intervention.
"It's a terrible thing, but thank goodness for a man that had a gun and knew how to use it," he said.
Without naming the bystander, Governor Kotek acknowledged the man's heroic actions stopping further loss of life, but noted they "carry a heavy emotional burden, and I just want you to know that my thoughts are with you as well".
Kayla Epstein contributed to this report.

A screenshot of an alleged post by former U.S. Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene criticizing President Donald Trump's "broken campaign promises" circulated on social media in October. The message found fault with Trump's handling of the Iran war and the Epstein files, and it accused him of "supporting, funding, and aiding genocide in Gaza."
(X user @TheresaAFallon)
Numerous readers emailed the screenshot to Snopes and asked us to verify that it was real.
The screenshot authentically showed a post by Greene.
She made the post in question on her official, verified social media channels on Facebook and X on Oct. 11.
The X post showed a timestamp of 2:54 p.m., while the Facebook post was posted about 20 minutes later, at 3:15 p.m.
We reached out to Greene for comment and will update this article if we hear back.
The post featured a screenshot of a standard Trump mailing list email featuring a Trump/Vance logo, to which Greene responded:
Oh he sent me an email, I think I'll respond.
So yes, actually you did do something wrong President Trump, let's first start with your broken campaign promises.
You protected your pedophile rapists friends instead of women who were raped when they were just teenage girls and you STILL REFUSE to release the Epstein files.
You started an unprovoked war with Iran that the vast majority of Americans do NOT support.
You killed hundreds of children at a school in Iran and innocent people and are responsible for 21 U.S. service members deaths and 865 wounded. Your stupid war that you claim you have won like 50 times has destroyed our bases in the Middle East and hundreds of billions of dollars worth of military equipment and weapons, while depleting our weapons and ammunitions.
You are supporting, funding, and aiding genocide in Gaza that has resulted in approximately 22,000 children murdered, thousands of children with amputations, and over 70,000 orphans.
And your so called Board of "Peace" has done nothing to stop war and is planning to oversee the very profitable reconstruction and take over of Gaza. One can only guess who all will get those blood money contracts, the Epstein class and associates.
And let's talk about the basics that every single US president is supposed to guarantee to its citizens. Affordable cost of living and affordable fuel in which you have 100% failed to deliver and actually driven inflation and irresponsibly driven the cost of gasoline and diesel to record high levels.
So did you do something wrong?
Yes in summary, YOU are the snake that you warned us all about in the poem you read over and over.
You never cared about putting America first or making America great again.
You are the deep state, the Epstein class, and America last.
And my mistake was supporting you in the first place.
Greene resigned from Congress in January after a widely reported break in her support for Trump.
In November, The Associated Press reported Greene had "increasingly dissented from Republican leaders, attacking them during the just-ended federal government shutdown and saying they need a plan to help people who are losing subsidies to afford health insurance policies."
The rift culminated in Greene criticizing Trump for the handling of the Epstein files and joining three other Republicans in support of a measure to force a vote on the Epstein Transparency Act, which became law in November.
Trump responded by calling Greene "wacky" and said her resignation was "good news" for the nation.
For further reading, Snopes previously investigated claims Greene was bribed to oppose Trump and that she bought shares of Palantir days before Immigration and Customs Enforcement announced a $30 million contract with the company.

UK should scrap ‘stupid’ ban on petrol cars to close EU trade deal, says Renault boss
The UK government has pledged to ban the sale of new petrol and diesel cars by 2030

The UK should get rid of a “stupid” ban on the sale of petrol and diesel cars in order to close a trade deal with the European Union, the chief of Renault has said.
Speaking to The Sunday Times, Renault CEO François Provost said if the UK wishes to join the EU’s Made in Europe industrial programme it should rethink the current pledge to ban the sale of petrol and diesel cars by 2030, while permitting hybrid car sales until 2035.
“What is a good date for 100 per cent electric?” Mr Provost said. “There is no good date because it’s stupid to ban non-electric cars. It is stupid.”
Downing Street has said inclusion in the EU’s Made in Europe scheme would be “good news” for Britain’s car industry, despite a report in The Guardian suggesting it would be conditional on Britain aligning with the EU’s position on tariffs for Chinese-made electric vehicles.
So far, Britain has resisted pressure from Europe to impose such tariffs, with trade secretary Jonathan Reynolds saying decisions on tariffs would be “based on the UK interest”.
But Mr Provost said the UK would need to fall in line with tariffs on Chinese imports if it wanted access to the scheme.
France and Germany have reportedly put forward a proposal to allow the UK’s automotive industry to be included in the protectionist scheme, known formally as the Industrial Accelerator Act.
Asked about the reports on Friday, a Number 10 spokesperson said the government would “welcome the objective to have the UK included in the Industrial Accelerator Act”.
She said it would be “good news for the British automotive industry and the jobs and investment it supports across the UK” but that there is “still a European process to run”.
Mr Provost said the UK’s automotive industry is at a “kind of tipping point”: “Obviously the UK has to be together with the EU. We have been in the same ecosystem for automotive for decades. So from a business perspective, from an industry perspective, this is just common sense.”
But he said industrial ambition for Europe’s car industry means being “realistic on electrification, but to continue electrification”, adding: “We have to freeze regulations now in order to decrease the price paid by customers.”
Andy Burnham warned earlier this week that the Made in Europe scheme presented “risks to British manufacturing” and promised to raise concerns about its impact on UK automotive firms with the bloc.
The programme is intended to protect clean technology firms and electric vehicle manufacturers from cheap Chinese competition.
The EU has already moved to limit imports of Chinese electric vehicles, including by imposing tariffs, and replicating those levies could be the price of the UK’s inclusion in Made in Europe.
The Department for Energy Security and Net Zero has been contacted for comment.

'It's really hard to believe' - How Oregon primary school shooting unfolded
Four victims, including a teacher and three children aged 5, 8 and 11, were killed in a shooting at a primary school in the US state of Oregon, local police say.
A 16-year-old suspect forced his way into the school by firing at locked doors. He was also killed in the shooting by an armed member of the community who followed the suspect inside the school, police said at a press conference.
Two additional victims, a 7-year-old and another teacher, were hurt and transported to hospital in critical condition.

Hours after Israeli militants attacked a delegation of European diplomats, French clerics and a visiting mayor in the occupied West Bank, Israel’s leader, Benjamin Netanyahu, responded by questioning the delegation’s account of the assault.
“Serious accusations require serious evidence” was the all-caps headline of a social media post from the office of the prime minister. As news of the attack spread globally there was no pledge to find those accountable and bring them to justice.
Instead Netanyahu’s team dismissed video of Bernard Baudoux, the mayor of Aulnoye-Aymeries in northern France, on the ground grimacing in pain and shock, photos of the smashed window of a diplomatic car, and footage of masked men threatening diplomats and activists with sticks.
“These images alone do not establish the complete sequence of events or individual responsibility,” the statement said, warning of “concerns about a coordinated campaign to smear Israel”.
The prime minister’s office went on to cast doubt on the integrity of senior French, Belgian and Polish diplomats in Jerusalem and clergy from the Catholic church who witnessed and reported the attack.
“We call on the public and responsible journalists to demand verifiable evidence, reject hearsay and refuse to turn unproven allegations into a collective indictment of the Jewish residents of Judea and Samaria [the occupied West Bank],” it said.
Guardian footage
Footage below filmed by the Guardian (no audio) shows the moments before Israeli settlers attacked the French mayor Bernard Baudoux, who was in the Palestinian town of Taybeh with a delegation of European diplomats. A second clip shows the immediate aftermath of the attack. The final section shows one group of settlers attacking the car carrying Baudoux and others.
Verifying the details of attacks can be painstaking journalistic work, seeking out eyewitness accounts, photos and videos for confirmation.
But this weekend the Guardian was in Taybeh, and witnessed the masked militants speeding up a hill in order to attack diplomats and French visitors who had spent a morning peacefully harvesting olives with Palestinians who own the groves.
Shortly after 1pm, they were warned that settlers had attacked Palestinians harvesting olives nearby. Keen to avoid confrontation, the group decided to leave and were approaching their vehicles as the militants closed in, masked, menacing and brandishing sticks.
The Guardian filmed the moments before Baudoux was assaulted, showing him approaching an SUV with his wife and Vincent Dollmann, the archbishop of Cambrai, escorted by diplomatic security. Our vehicle pulled away, making room for the two parked by the road to follow.
Moments later the settlers attacked, apparently determined not only to force the foreigners to flee but to extract a price for joining Palestinians on their land.
It was clear the group contained foreign dignitaries because the cars had diplomatic plates, and Baudoux was apparently targeted for his nationality, because he was wearing his mayor’s sash of office. One of the attackers aggressively shouted “France, France” before pushing him to the ground, eyewitnesses said.
Metadata from that video shows there were just 22 seconds between the last shot of Baudoux remonstrating with his attackers and footage of him slumped on the ground taken by activists in the second car.
The embassy security team then helped him into the vehicle but the attack continued as they drove off. Footage filmed from the hillside opposite shows the settlers attacking the SUV as pulls away.
The force of their blows smashed one of the reinforced windows at the back of the car, which can be seen intact in the first video. A photo of the crumpled pane taken minutes later in the relative safety of Taybeh shows the force of the impact.
If the militant settlers had broken one of the windows next to the passengers, it is unlikely those inside would have escaped injuries.
Israeli authorities have repeatedly attempted to obfuscate details of attacks on Palestinians and undermine survivor or witness accounts.
For the prime minister to deploy the same tactics on senior diplomats from European allies – however strained their current relationship – marks a new embrace of isolationist extremism.
A day earlier the American photojournalist Heidi Levine was hospitalised after a brutal attack by Israeli militants blocking the Palestinian olive harvest in another village. Netanyahu’s office described it as an “alleged assault” and a “disputed incident” adding “the facts … remain unclear and are under investigation”.
The message from the very top of Israel’s government, that the state was reluctant to impose consequences or seek justice for that attack, may have emboldened the attackers on Saturday.
There was one unprecedented response in Jerusalem, however. On Sunday, more than a dozen of Israel’s top former diplomats gathered outside the foreign ministry where they had all worked for decades for an unprecedented protest.
Two former directors general, one deputy director general and a host of ambassadors held up signs calling for action on the campaign of terror by Israelis against Palestinians in the occupied West Bank.
“Bibi [Netanyahu], foreign minister [Gideon] Sa’ar. Stop Jewish Terrorism. It’s in your hands,” read one banner.

‘Birthday vacation in Paris?’ Opposition questions Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann’s France trip
Some opposition leaders alleged Mann was taking his wife along on the trip to celebrate his birthday.
Chief minister Bhagwant Mann’s France visit has set off a political controversy in Punjab, with the Opposition alleging that he left for a foreign tour at a time when the state faces a grave drug crisis and the family of an anti-drug activist awaits justice.
Some opposition leaders also alleged Mann was taking his wife along on the trip to celebrate his birthday. Mann turned 53 on Saturday.
The tour is in connection with participation of the Punjab State Cooperative Supply and Marketing Federation Ltd. (MARKFED), the apex cooperative of the state, in the international food trade show, SIAL 2026, in Paris from October 17 to October 21. The MARKFED was allotted a stall in the India Pavilion by the Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority (APEDA) – a body under the Union ministry of commerce and industry.
Mann was to lead a delegation which would also comprise the chief secretary and the principal secretary to the chief minister.
Also read | ‘Political angle’ not explained while denying clearance for Mann's France visit, says HC on Centre’s call
"An Evening in Paris. Punjab suffers in turmoil and the grieving family of martyr Jhota still awaits justice," Shiromani Akali Dal leader Bikram Singh Majithia said.
Majithia was referring to the murder of anti-drug activist Parvinder Singh Jhota in broad daylight inside a medical store at a busy market place in Mansa on October 13. Jhota was known for raising his voice against the illegal sale of addictive substances at chemist shops. Ashwani Kumar, the store owner who opened fire on Jhota after he questioned him for selling addictive drugs to an elderly man, was taken into custody from Salasar in Rajasthan.
Senior Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leader Tarun Chugh alleged Mann was going on a "family trip" to France to celebrate his birthday on the pretext of setting up the MARKFED stall when Punjab is reeling under heavy financial crisis.
Government employees are crying for dearness allowance and gangsters are ruining the state, but this "fun trip" of Bhagwant Mann is "making fun" of Punjab and its people, he alleged.
Also read | Row erupts as Centre seeks report from Punjab on drug-linked killings, ‘suicide’
He also hit out at the ruling Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) over the drug menace, saying: “At a time Punjab is burning in the fire of drug abuse, Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann is heading for France with his wife to celebrate his birthday instead of addressing the suffering of the people.”
He added: "The chief minister's conduct amid such a grave crisis raises serious questions about the government's priorities and its sensitivity towards the people of Punjab.”
Punjab is gripped by fear and insecurity, yet the chief minister appears more concerned about his foreign trip than confronting this crisis, he said.
He also alleged that a birthday celebration is being projected as an official government tour.
"What kind of official delegation includes the chief minister's wife? What is the justification for her participation?" he asked.
Chugh said taxpayers' money must not be used to finance private celebrations or family leisure trips.
Also read | Trade promotion tour: Punjab govt moves HC as Centre denies clearance for France visit
Former Union minister and BJP leader Ravneet Singh Bittu posted on X: “Paris Official Visit or Birthday Vacation?”
He continued: "Bhagwant Mann's birthday trip to Paris -- in whose name, and at whose expense," he asked. "Punjab's treasury is not a family holiday fund! Bhagwant Mann must disclose the purpose, expenses and official invitation.”
There was no immediate reaction either from the chief minister or the AAP at the time of filing this report.
On Friday, the Punjab and Haryana high court allowed the Punjab government's plea challenging the Centre's decision to deny political clearance for Mann for his visit to France.
The Punjab government moved the court, saying the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA)'s decision was "arbitrary" and sought the decision to be quashed.
The high court questioned the Centre’s decision to deny the clearance, observing that a “political angle” cited as the reason for the denial had not been explained.
“It has not been explained what that political angle/viewpoint is, and whether political clearance means examining the application from a political angle. No reasons are forthcoming,” the high court remarked. Taking note of a September 22 communication from the event organiser, the court also did not find substance in the Centre’s argument that there was lack of a proper invitation from the French government.

At least 34 schoolchildren and a female teacher have died after the roof of a school collapsed during morning classes in the northern Pakistani city of Peshawar.
As panicked parents and relatives thronged the site of the privately run al-Khair school to search for their loved ones, rescue workers spent hours pulling children from the rubble.
Most of the victims were under 13 years old and from low-income households. At least 45 children suffered injuries, ranging from minor wounds to severe trauma, said Arif Khattak, the regional director of emergency services.
Television footage showed rescuers clawing through debris with their bare hands and carrying bloodied children to waiting ambulances as people crowded the alley where the school stood.
The roof of a higher floor collapsed on to classrooms below, crumpling two storeys of the building, a rescue official said. “The fatalities include 12 girl students and a female teacher,” said the Lady Reading hospital spokesperson, Mohammad Asim. Three children remained in critical condition with head injuries, while most of the injured taken to the hospital had been treated and discharged, he added.
The incident took place at 8.48am local time (0348 GMT) and the rescue operation lasted for four to five hours, Khattak said. “It was a weak building structure,” said the Peshawar police chief, Mian Saeed. “Its roof was overloaded with construction on a weak structure, which caused the collapse.”
Saeed said the school’s owner had been arrested and an investigation launched. A total of 110 students were attending lessons in three classrooms when the roof caved in.
Distraught relatives accused the school of ignoring concerns about the building’s condition and demanded accountability. “Make an example of them, a lesson for all, so that no one dares open a school just to make money without providing facilities,” said Mohammad Zaman, who lost two nephews in the collapse.
The school was located in a poor, crowded neighbourhood of Peshawar, the capital of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province, where Pakistan’s president imposed a state of emergency on Sunday, saying the provincial government had failed to tackle Islamist militancy from neighbouring Afghanistan, an allegation it denied.
Pakistan spends less than 1% of its approximately $450bn (£340bn) GDP on education, leaving many families dependent on low-cost private schools.
Many of those schools operate from poorly maintained rented buildings with limited oversight, contributing to recurring safety concerns. In June, at least 14 children died when the roof of a tutoring centre housed in a dilapidated building collapsed in the eastern city of Lahore.
There was no immediate comment from school officials.
The country’s prime minister, Shehbaz Sharif, expressed sorrow over the tragedy and offered condolences to the victims’ families, his office said.
Jawad Ahmad, whose son and daughter survived the incident, said the news had left him devastated. “It felt as if someone had shot me in the chest when I learned that the school building had collapsed,” he said.
The province, governed for years by the party of the jailed former prime minister Imran Khan, has frequently been at odds with the federal administration. Pakistan’s president, Asif Ali Zardari, imposed a new governor on the province when he declared the state of emergency on Sunday, sharpening the tensions.
