Mr Roland Driece, Director for International Relations at the Netherlands’ Ministry of Health, Welfare and Sport, Mr Gerard Steeghs, Director Multilateral Organisations and Human Rights, Dr Catharina Boehme, Chef de Cabinet, WHO
Geneva, 17 November 2022 – The Netherlands discussed its new strategy for Global Health with WHO on Thursday and called for deeper coordination with the Organization to improve global health – aiming to strengthen health systems at home and worldwide, better prepare for pandemics and address the impact of climate change on public health.
The presentation of the Dutch Global Health Strategy 2023-2030: “Working together for health worldwide” came during a full day of strategic dialogue in which WHO and the Netherlands reflected on their longstanding partnership and set a way forward for their shared priorities.
Led by Mr Gerard Steeghs, Director Multilateral Organisations and Human Rights, Mr Joris Jurriëns, Head of the Health and AIDS Division at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and Mr Roland Driece, Director for International Relations at the Netherlands’ Ministry of Health, Welfare and Sport, the delegation indicated that in the coming year, the Netherlands will scale up its efforts in the field of global health through the new Strategy with WHO and other health organizations, like the Global Fund and UNAIDS.
The Strategy aims to contribute in a coordinated and targeted way to improving public health around the world, including in the Netherlands. Stressing its excellent partnership with WHO, the Netherlands welcomed the opportunity to strengthen the collaboration through the new Strategy.
On Thursday, the Netherlands also announced its intention to provide solid, predictable, mostly flexible, multi-year financing to WHO, building on its longstanding support of the Organization. This commitment consolidates the Netherlands’ position as a top contributor of flexible funds – resources that enable a stronger result driven WHO to fulfil its mandate and work most effectively for the health of everyone.
From new conflicts to resurging diseases, the global community faces increasingly complex health challenges. Against this backdrop, WHO highlighted the role of the Netherlands as a courageous partner, advocating for equal access to health services to all people, including on Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights, and welcomed its renewed commitment to global health under the new Strategy.
"Your voice, your advocacy for other countries – even in times of shrinking economies and difficult crises, to keep the focus on global health – are of critical importance, and WHO looks forward to working with you as you go ahead with this brave global health strategy,” WHO Chef de Cabinet Dr Catharina Boehme said.
The meeting touched on shared priorities in strengthening national health systems, access to medicines and local manufacturing, planet health – including One Health – as well as antimicrobial resistance, environmental health, and health and human rights, including access to sexual and reproductive health for all girls and women.
Joining forces to promote equitable access to medicines and other health technologies, Mr Driece and Dr Mariângela Batista Galvão Simão, WHO Assistant Director-General, Access to Medicines and Health Products, signed a letter of intent to co-host the second edition of the World Local Production Forum in June 2023. The Forum draws high-level, global attention and sparks discussions on challenges and opportunities related to local production of pharmaceuticals, vaccines and other health products.
WHO also welcomed the Netherlands’ support for WHO’s work on health emergencies, including the country’s engagement in international negotiations towards a pandemic accord. The Netherlands collaboration with WHO boosts pandemic preparedness and response, and builds the world’s health architecture with WHO at the centre.
-----------------
The Netherlands is a key supporter and strategic partner of WHO. It funds crucial activities in the areas of sexual and reproductive health, water and sanitation, mental health in emergencies, emergency preparedness, tuberculosis, One Health, primary health care, antimicrobial resistance, while facilitating cooperation with top Dutch institutions.
Between 2020 and 2021, the Netherlands provided over US$ 94 million to WHO, including US$ 16 million in fully flexible core voluntary contributions, making it the fourth-largest flexible contributor to the Organization. Such support allows WHO to be agile and strategic in its efforts to reach the Triple Billion targets and help countries improve the health and well-being of their populations.
The Netherlands is also the fourth-largest contributor to WHO’s Contingency Fund for Emergencies, which enables WHO to respond rapidly to disease outbreaks and other health emergencies around the world.

Kolkata stampede: Mamata faction alleges Durga Puja pandal panel has ‘links’ to CM's nephew, BJP hits back
The allegations came even as seven people were arrested.
The Opposition on Sunday targeted the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) government in West Bengal over the deadly stampede inside a Durga Puja pandal in Kolkata, alleging attempts are being made to shield the organisers, most of whom are from the ruling party.
The Mamata All India Trinamool Congress (MAITC) alleged the puja committee – Chore Bagan Sarbojanin Durgatsav Samity – has links to Adhikari’s nephew Debdeep Adhikari and sought to know when he would be arrested.
The allegations came even as seven people were arrested and chief minister Suvendu Adhikari announced the formation of a Special Investigation Team headed by a sitting judge of the Calcutta high court to probe the stampede.

Deep Dive
MAITC spokesperson and Kolkata MLA Kunal Ghosh alleged the administration had failed to prevent the stampede and called on the organisers to take responsibility.
“This accident is a complete failure of the administration, and the concerned Puja Committee must take responsibility for it. There are many influential individuals involved, but right now, we are at the hospital. Since yesterday evening, our priority has been relief work and medical treatment,” he said.
He alleged the chief minister’s statement was “incomplete, an evasion of responsibility, misleading, and an attempt to divert attention”. “The committee's officials must be arrested immediately. The municipal corporation and OSD must be removed. An impartial investigation is needed. The committee is filled with BJP members. They are being shielded. It didn't rain for the first time today. Blaming just the rain is an attempt to cover up administrative failure," he said.
The stampede occurred around 7.30pm on Saturday at Chor Bagan, one of the city’s most popular Durga Puja venues, in cramped north Kolkata, as crowds jostled through a narrow bylane on Saptami, the seventh day of the festival, even as rain lashed the city and left the streets slippery.
Ghosh posted a purported letter by the Chore Bagan Sarbojanin – the puja committee organiser – on X, alleging the panel’s previous members were forced to step down after the BJP came to power in May.
“In Chorbagan, the previous committee was forced to resign, and a new committee 'took over'. Take a look at the resignation letter from the former committee and see who the members of the new committee are,” he said in a post in Bengali on X.

The purported letter by Jayanta Banerjee, the general secretary of the old committee, on July 17 said he and seven other committee members were stepping down. HT could not independently verify the authenticity of the letter.
Chore Bagan is a part of the Jorasanko Assembly constituency, which BJP's Jijay Ojha won in May after defeating TMC's Vijay Upadhyay.
Ojha is the chairman of the new committee. Speaking to reporters after visiting the spot on Sunday, he said: "I am also on the committee. The chief minister has ordered a probe.”
Asked if he was aware that the entry and exit routes to this year's pandal appeared to be too narrow as per safety standards, he said he was not aware of it.
MAITC general secretary Abhishek Banerjee said allegations were raised about chief minister Adhikari’s nephew’s purported link with the puja committee. He also alleged the involvement of BJP’s north Kolkata unit president Tamoghna Ghosh in the puja pandal arrangements.
"When are you putting the guilty nephew in jail Suvendu babu?" Banerjee said in a post on Facebook.
Raising doubts that Ojha, Ghosh and the chief minister's nephew would likely be spared, Banerjee said Adhikari must carry out his constitutional role as an administrator.
Hitting back, state BJP spokesperson and MLA from the adjacent Kashipur-Belgachhia constituency Ritesh Tiwari said: “I do not know if any relative of the chief minister is linked to the puja committee but even if he was, would he ever want such a tragedy to take place under his watch?”
He added: "For decades, TMC leaders such as Partha Chatterjee, Aroop Biswas and Firhad Hakim have been closely associated with the community Durga Pujas. Some BJP leaders may also have been associated with some pujas. What is wrong with that?”
Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi also condemned the incident and called for a fair probe. “The news of the stampede at the Chorbagan Puja pandal in Kolkata is extremely heartbreaking. Reports indicate that several people have lost their lives in this tragedy, and a large number of people have been injured. My deepest condolences to the families of the deceased. I pray for the swift recovery of the injured,” he said in a post on X.
“I appeal to the administration to ensure that all the injured receive immediate and proper medical treatment, and that a fair investigation into this incident is conducted so that such a tragedy is never repeated in the future. I appeal to Congress workers to provide every possible assistance in the relief efforts,” he added.
BJP MLA Sajal Ghosh said “it would be premature to pinpoint exactly where the error lies”. “We must acknowledge that mistakes can occur. Had it not been for the rain, perhaps we would not have had to face such an incident. Regardless, there is no attempt to hide anything,” he said.

California Gov. Gavin Newsom addressed the growing controversy involving his former wife, Kimberly Guilfoyle, on Saturday, offering a brief response when questioned while campaigning for Democratic candidates in New Hampshire.
When CBS News reporter Jared Ochacher asked Newsom for his reaction to Guilfoyle’s recent departure from her position as U.S. ambassador to Greece following allegations of misconduct, Newsom paused and rubbed his eyes before answering.
“I don’t know enough about it,” Newsom said. “I haven’t talked to her in a while. I just wish her the best, and I don’t have much, honestly, much more to say on it. It’s unfortunate.”
The comments mark the first time Newsom, a prominent critic of President Donald Trump, has publicly addressed the scandal surrounding Guilfoyle.
Guilfoyle’s departure from her diplomatic post followed allegations made by former Kentucky congressional candidate Eric Deters. Deters released text messages he alleged were between himself and Guilfoyle, claiming she offered access to the Trump family in exchange for payment of her $100,000 American Express bill.
Guilfoyle denied the allegations, claiming the messages were doctored, though additional allegations of cash-for-access schemes later emerged.
Her firing was announced on live television on Tuesday by then-White House Press Secretary Katie Zacharia during her first press conference. Zacharia was dismissed from her position five days into the role.
Guilfoyle was appointed to the ambassadorial role after maintaining ties with the administration following her breakup with Donald Trump Jr. The couple was engaged from 2020 until 2024, ending their relationship amid reports involving Palm Beach socialite Bettina Anderson.
Donald Trump Jr. and Anderson married on May 21 in the Bahamas during a three-day event reportedly funded by Russian oligarch Umar Kremlev. Donald Trump, who did not attend the ceremony, later stated that his son had reimbursed Kremlev for the costs of the event.
Newsom and Guilfoyle originally met at a political event in 1994 and married in December 2001. They filed for divorce in January 2005, and the separation was finalized in February 2006.

As Chuck Lorre‘s memoir continues to make the rounds, Tom Arnold is the latest sitcom actor to respond to criticisms of himself in the book.
Following Lorre’s claim in Sitcom that writers on Roseanne (1988-’97) were told to “put Tom’s name on the front page [of scripts]—as if Tom had written them,” Arnold emphasized that he “never would put my name on a script” that he didn’t write, recounting from his perspective “how it went on the show.”
“Roseanne and I sat around talking about what we wanted to do in the next season, or maybe some ideas we had that’d be fun episodes, or groundbreaking, or whatever our bullsh*t was, and I’d write them down,” explained Arnold to Entertainment Weekly. “We kind of doodled around. And then, you know, in probably June, the head writer and the writers would come back and the show starts shooting in August.”
Arnold noted that after breaking the story with the writers’ room, no matter whose name was on the script, it had “every writer’s fingerprints on it.”
Watch on Deadline
“They all work on everything,” he explained. “Even the guys that are brought in to be the punch-up guys, the joke guys, everybody in the room at some point is pitching different things.”
Serving as a producer on Seasons 3-6, during which he had a recurring guest spot as Arnie Thomas, Arnold recalled he “didn’t realize Chuck was having such a hard time, because it seemed to go pretty well. There’s nothing outstanding.”
“I know one thing I said to Chuck early on… I said, ‘You’re in charge of the writers, but they have to have their name on a script every year. Each one of these guys,'” he noted. “Because you get more money, you just get more. I want everybody to have their name on a script. We’ll write extra scripts, whatever we gotta do.”
Arnold continued, “One friend that I really made a point, a guy named Joel Madison, who I just talked to, I don’t think Chuck liked him because he did not give him a script. It was two weeks before we were done, and I found out. I go, ‘Hey, Chuck, you’ve gotta give Joel a script. I told you you had to do that.’ He said, ‘Oh, shoot. Yeah, well, all I’ve got is this one with my name on it.’ I go, ‘Put Joel’s name on it. You’re the head writer, you make a lot of money, put his name.'”
Lorre, who was a writer and producer on Roseanne in Seasons 3 and 4, claimed in his memoir that writer Danny Jacobson once “showed me a sloppy, hand-scribbled couple of pages and explained this was a ‘script’ by the show’s new executive producer, Tom Arnold. It had been part of Danny’s job to write real scripts and put Tom’s name on the front page—as if Tom had written them.”
The 10x Emmy nominee alleged that “several other staff writers would be ordered to do this on many occasions,” which Jacobson confirmed to EW, claiming that Arnold’s then wife Roseanne “bullied me into letting him write a script, which as Chuck described, was exactly right. So it was really — it was a bad energy on the show.”

Hong Kong ‘optimistic’ on economic growth despite global slowdown, Paul Chan says
The finance chief says city is well placed to channel global capital, support mainland Chinese firms going abroad and fund AI infrastructure in developing economies
Hong Kong is more “optimistic” about its economic growth this year than the International Monetary Fund (IMF) is about the global outlook, the finance chief has said, pointing to the city’s unique position to capitalise on international capital flows and the artificial intelligence (AI) boom.
Writing on his blog on Sunday after attending the IMF and World Bank Group’s annual meetings in Bangkok, Financial Secretary Paul Chan Mo-po said world leaders’ discussions had been dominated by two forces: the rapid disruption driven by AI and energy price surges stemming from conflicts in the Middle East.
He noted that while the IMF expected global growth to slow from 3.5 per cent last year to 3.1 per cent this year, Asia’s economy would continue to expand at a faster pace.
The IMF recently upgraded its 2026 real GDP growth forecast for Hong Kong to 3.8 per cent, while the local government maintained its full-year forecast at 3.5 to 4.5 per cent.

Adani Group chairman Gautam Adani and Adani Foundation chairperson Dr Priti Adani visited Shrimad Rajchandra Mission Dharampur (SRMD) in South Gujarat on Sunday during Navratri, where they sought the blessings of Pujya Gurudevshri Rakeshji.
Sharing details of the visit on X, Gautam Adani wrote, "Priti and I spent warm moments with Pujya Gurudevshri Rakeshji at Shrimad Rajchandra Ashram, Dharampur, and received His blessings. Performing charan pakshal at the world's tallest idol of Shrimad Rajchandraji was deeply moving."
During the meeting, Pujya Gurudevshri highlighted the connection between saadhana (spiritual practice) and seva (selfless service). He also discussed the importance of directing one's life, resources and opportunities towards the larger good.
The couple attended a satsang (association with truth) at Raj Sabhagruha, SRMD's meditation and spiritual discourse complex. The session focused on the purpose of human life and the significance of spiritual practice.
Adani also interacted with young members of the Mission, including professionals and students from varied academic backgrounds who are involved in its social initiatives.
Dr Priti Adani visited the Shrimad Rajchandra Sarvamangal Centre of Excellence for Women, where she met tribal women participating in skill development, livelihood and entrepreneurship programmes.
She also visited Shrimad Rajchandra Hospital and Research Centre and took part in the distribution of medical aids to children with disabilities. At SRMD's Jinmandir, she offered prayers to Bhagwan Mahavir.
The visit also included discussions on potential cooperation between the Adani Foundation and Shrimad Rajchandra Love and Care (SRLC), the Mission's humanitarian arm. Gautam Adani expressed interest in exploring collaborations with SRLC, while Dr Priti Adani discussed the possibility of working together on its vision care initiative, which aligns with the Adani Foundation's work.
Spread across 355 acres, Shrimad Rajchandra Ashram serves as the international headquarters of SRMD. Founded in 1994 by Pujya Gurudevshri Rakeshji, the Mission has more than 142 centres across six continents.
The organisation draws inspiration from Shrimad Rajchandraji, the Jain master revered as Mahatma Gandhi's spiritual mentor. Its teachings focus on inner transformation through wisdom, meditation and selfless service.
SRLC, the Mission's humanitarian arm, works across healthcare, education, humanitarian assistance, animal care and environmental welfare. Its initiatives have reached millions of people globally.
Earlier this year, Gautam Adani visited Ayodhya, Kalighat in Kolkata and a Jain shrine at Taranga Hills in North Gujarat.
On 1 May, he visited Kedarnath with Dr Priti Adani to mark their 40th wedding anniversary.

Save-On-Foods loyalty program members had personal information accessed in cybersecurity breach
Names were accessed, possibly contact information and addresses, but no number on how many affected
A major Canadian supermarket chain has notified customers in its loyalty program that their personal information was accessed during a cybersecurity breach.
The Western Canadian grocery chain Save-On-Foods says it discovered unauthorized activity on one of its servers on Oct. 13, which was "quickly contained" before launching an investigation with a cybersecurity expert.
An email was then sent out to More Rewards customers Friday.
"We are writing to let you know about an incident involving your personal information," the email read.
Customers who received an email were told that their names and — if provided — addresses, phone numbers, email addresses and dates of birth were accessed.
CBC News asked Save-On-Foods how many customers were affected in the data breach but did not receive a number by deadline.
Save-On-Foods requires online shoppers to be signed up for the More Rewards program, which also offers members exclusive in-store discounts.
The email said "based on the information available," no other personal information, such as credit card data or passwords, was accessed.
Phishing concerns
However, the Canadian Centre for Cyber Security says personal information can be used by cybercriminals to make phishing attacks more convincing, impersonating trusted organizations to trick people into sharing sensitive information or sending money.
"Most of these break-ins are opportunistic," wrote Richard Frank, director of Simon Fraser University’s international cybercrime centre, in an email to CBC News.
He said criminals often gain access to corporate networks through employees accidentally clicking malicious links or downloading malware.
But that’s when criminals can "map the network," identify whatever they can steal to monetize, "and loyalty programs usually provide enough details to make realistic scams."
Frank explained that personal information is often used by cybercriminals to impersonate companies in emails requesting more information or containing malicious links, potentially allowing them to steal identities, banking information or credit card details.
He said criminals can use that more sensitive information to make fraudulent purchases through online stores and even cryptomarkets.
Community response
Numerous Reddit commenters on B.C. and Alberta sub-communities expressed frustration with discount systems that require customers to provide personal information through loyalty programs, arguing data like that can be sold corporately and makes them a target for cybercrime.
Several of those subreddit posts suggest that customers who received the notification and then tried to change their passwords were met with a recurring error.
More Rewards members are being told to be vigilant about suspicious calls or messages, as Save-On-Foods says it will not send any communications asking for passwords, banking information, payment information, social insurance numbers or security question answers.
In an email to CBC News, Save-On-Foods said it notified the appropriate authorities and privacy regulators.
CBC News reached out to the Office of the Information and Privacy Commissioner for B.C. to confirm whether it had been notified of the incident but did not hear back before publication.

- Assassin's Creed Destiny was a reportedly cancelled game set in ancient China in 206 BCE.
- The project featured a female assassin, gameplay centered around stealth, and a glimpse of a boss fight.
- Due to the internal team restructuring, Destiny remains cancelled.
The Assassin’s Creed franchise could have taken players on another adventure through ancient China, but the unannounced project never made it to release. Newly surfaced gameplay footage and screenshots have revealed Assassin’s Creed Destiny, a cancelled game developed by a Tencent-owned branch in collaboration with Ubisoft.
The footage shows a female assassin infiltrating a military palace, fighting the guards, and hunting for a mysterious artifact. According to a report by MP1st, the project was set during China’s Qin Dynasty in 206 BCE.
Most of the footage comes from a February 2025 prototype that reveals stealth combat, parkour, the iconic Leap of Faith, and an unusual Umbrella-inspired weapon. The project was cancelled following the restructuring of TiMi, the Tencent branch.
Leaked footage shows Assassin’s Creed Destiny was planned as a massive historical adventure, not a mobile spin-off like Jade. An early version of the boss encounter involving Xiang Yu, a Chinese warlord, also appears in the leaks. The footage raises an important question about Ubisoft’s broader plans since it is reportedly working on Assassin’s Creed Hexe, which takes a different approach from the RPG formula.
Beyond the mission of finding the artifact, the footage showcases the familiar Assassin’s Creed mechanics, including stealth takedowns, parkour, and navigating through the palace. One distinctive detail is the spinning umbrella weapon, along with the ability icons inspired by the ink-brush artwork, and HUD icons inspired by the Yin-Yang symbol.
While there is no concrete evidence about why Assassin’s Creed Destiny was cancelled, reports point towards a team restructuring for TiMi and Tencent’s broader shift away from Western partnerships to releasing casual experiences locally.
Although Assassin’s Creed Destiny is off the table, Assassin’s Creed Jade still stays in development. For other projects, fans must keep an eye out for the late 2027 release window for Assassin’s Creed Hexe. It is yet to be seen what other ideas Ubisoft has in their minds after the cancelled game set in China.

New Delhi, Oct 18: The Supreme Court has expressed displeasure over states and Union territories not responding to the Centre on how its judgment declaring menstrual hygiene as a part of the fundamental right under Article 21 of the Constitution is being implemented.
“If what we have said in the judgment is only going to remain on paper, how is the Union, states/UTs going to give effect to this fundamental right?” a bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and R Mahadevan said.
It said the apex court had declared menstrual hygiene/menstrual health as one of the facets of Article 21 of the Constitution, which deals with the protection of life and personal liberty.
The bench said that on September 1, it had directed the states and UTs to take into consideration the deficiencies highlighted by it and report in that regard by the next date of hearing.
In a significant judgment delivered on January 30, the apex court said that the right to life under Article 21 of the Constitution includes the right to menstrual health.
During the hearing in the matter on October 13, Additional Solicitor General Aishwarya Bhati, appearing for the Centre, told the bench that the Union of India has taken up this issue very seriously with all the states and UTs to respond in what manner the judgment is being implemented.
“Unfortunately, the states/UTs have not responded to the Union so far. We fail to understand that once the Union calls for the necessary information, why the states/UTs do not respond,” the bench said.
“We are sure that the Union, the states/UTs have realised the importance of the judgment that we delivered, declaring menstrual hygiene as a part of the fundamental right,” it said.
The bench said the apex court's verdict was in the interest of young girls who were giving up education, more particularly, in remote parts of the country because of the problem of menstrual hygiene, etc.
“We direct the Union to take up this issue very seriously with each state/UT and call for the necessary information in writing as to what steps they have taken so far for giving effect to the judgment delivered by this court,” it said.
The bench said the Centre should study the verdict once again and accordingly call for information on each and every aspect of the matter.
“On the next date of hearing, if we hear from the Union that some of the states/UTs have not responded, we shall proceed to issue contempt notice to the concerned chief secretary,” the bench said.
While granting one last opportunity to do the needful, it posted the matter for next hearing on December 14.
In its September 1 order, the bench had said the focus should be on the number of schools that lack gender-segregated, functional toilets with usable water connectivity, ensuring accessibility and privacy.
The Centre had then informed the top court that 30,458 gender-segregated toilets with washing facilities have been constructed in schools across the country while 4,236 were under construction.
In its judgment delivered in January, the apex court had directed the states and UTs to ensure that every school, whether government-run or privately managed, in both urban and rural areas, was provided with functional, gender-segregated toilets with usable water connectivity.
The top court had also directed the states and UTs to ensure that every school provides sanitary napkins to girl students free of cost.
The judgment was delivered on a plea seeking pan-India implementation of the Centre’s ‘menstrual hygiene policy for schoolgoing girls’ in government and government-aided schools from classes 6 to 12.

The death of actor Nana Patekar, 75, has drawn attention to coronary thrombosis, a condition in which a blood clot forms in an artery supplying the heart. What causes these clots, who is at risk, and how is the condition diagnosed and treated?
The story so far:
According to published accounts of the autopsy report, actor Nana Patekar died after a blood clot blocked the left main coronary artery, which supplies blood to a large part of the heart muscle. A blockage in this artery can severely restrict blood flow to the heart and cause a heart attack. The reported finding has drawn attention to coronary thrombosis, the formation of a blood clot within a coronary artery.
What is coronary thrombosis?
Coronary thrombosis occurs when a blood clot forms in one of the arteries that supply blood to the heart muscle. These arteries carry oxygen and nutrients that the heart needs to function. When a clot partly or completely blocks an artery, less blood reaches the heart muscle. If the blood supply is cut off for too long, the heart muscle can become damaged, leading to a heart attack. The severity depends on how much of the artery is blocked and how quickly blood flow is restored.
This form of thrombosis is often associated with atherosclerosis, in which fatty deposits, cholesterol and other substances build up in the artery walls. These deposits, called plaques, can remain unnoticed for years.
When a plaque ruptures or its surface is eroded, platelets gather at the site and a clot may form. The clot can then obstruct blood flow, sometimes suddenly. Damage to the inner surface of an artery can trigger the process of clot formation. Additionally, at rupture, the material beneath the plaque’s surface comes into contact with blood, prompting platelets to gather and the clotting process to begin. A clot may grow quickly and block the artery.
What are the warning signs?
A clot that significantly restricts blood flow through a coronary artery may cause chest discomfort, pressure or tightness. Pain may spread to the arms, shoulders, back, neck or jaw. Breathlessness, sweating, nausea, dizziness and unusual fatigue may also occur.
The symptoms depend on the artery affected and the extent of the blockage. Some people may have less typical symptoms or no obvious warning signs before the blockage becomes serious. Symptoms alone cannot confirm coronary thrombosis; medical assessment and investigations are needed.
Suspected coronary artery blockage accompanied by chest pain or breathlessness requires emergency medical attention.
Who is at risk?
People living with coronary artery disease are at greater risk of coronary thrombosis because fatty deposits can build up in their arteries and trigger clot formation if a deposit ruptures. Smoking, high blood pressure, high LDL cholesterol, diabetes, physical inactivity and an unhealthy diet can increase the risk of developing this artery disease.
In some cases, a clot may form in an artery affected by other conditions, including inflammation or injury to the blood vessel.
Older age and a family history of heart disease at a younger age are also risk factors. However it can occur even in people who have not been diagnosed with coronary artery disease. The underlying plaque build-up may have gone undetected until it triggers the formation of a clot.
How is this condition diagnosed?
Doctors assess symptoms and medical history and use tests to determine whether a coronary artery is blocked and whether the heart muscle has been damaged. An electrocardiogram (ECG) records the heart’s electrical activity, while blood tests measuring cardiac troponin can help identify damage to the heart muscle.
Coronary angiography uses a contrast dye and X-rays to show the coronary arteries and identify the location and extent of a blockage. This can help doctors decide how best to restore blood flow. Other tests may be used depending on the patient’s condition.
How is it treated?
Treatment aims to restore blood flow and prevent the clot from growing or new clots from forming. The approach depends on the location and severity of the blockage and the patient’s condition.
Angioplasty may be used to reopen the affected artery. A thin tube is guided to the blockage, where a small balloon is inflated to widen the artery. A stent, a small mesh tube, is often placed to help keep it open.
Doctors may also use antiplatelet medicines, which reduce the tendency of platelets to clump together, and anticoagulants, which interfere with the blood-clotting process. In selected cases, clot-dissolving medicines may be used. Coronary artery bypass surgery may be considered when the pattern of blockage makes it a more suitable option.
Preventing further clots involves managing the underlying risk factors and following the prescribed treatment plan. This may include controlling blood pressure, cholesterol and blood sugar, stopping tobacco use, maintaining physical activity appropriate to the person’s condition and taking prescribed medicines.

Delhi Police detained journalists for a second consecutive day on Sunday, October 11, while they covered the protest called by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and Left-wing student outfits demanding the resignation of chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Journalists from mainstream outlets and independent houses were among those held, and several said they were detained even after showing press credentials. The detentions came on the same day the Supreme Court said lawyers, journalists and other professionals must not be hindered in their duties “in any manner whatsoever.”
Three journalists from Indian Express Hindi, Shashwat, Siya and Vijay, were among those detained. The organisation said on X that the three told police they were journalists doing their job but were forcibly put into a bus. It said Shashwat sent a video he recorded on his phone as the bus passed through Connaught Place, and that Siya’s phone was seized by police. The three were later released at Chhatrasal Stadium, the organisation said.

As nearly a hundred activists and protesters marched towards Connaught Place, security personnel closed in, barricaded roads and prevented others from joining. At Connaught Place, journalists were stopped from recording as police and CRPF personnel pushed protesters into buses. Suresh was among those detained and taken away in a police vehicle. According to her own narration, she remained in detention until late into the night.
A photojournalist working for a news agency told The Times of India that he was covering the All India Student Association (AISA) protest at R K Ashram Marg when police began dispersing people. The van held seven or eight journalists when its doors were shut and it moved off. After a few kilometres it had to stop because police were removing barricades, and he and two others jumped out. The photojournalist was not named in the report.
The Supreme Court’s Order
In a special hearing on Sunday morning, Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana sought responses from Union home secretary Govind Mohan, Delhi police commissioner Anurag Kumar and Delhi Metro chief D Thara on a contempt petition alleging a prima facie violation of the court’s October 9 order against a complete shutdown of Metro and train services on Saturday. The bench said the petitioners had made out a prima facie case, and it asked for responses by October 13.
The court also asked for internet connectivity to be normalised and said there must be no illegal detentions, particularly of peaceful, unarmed gatherings beyond areas where Section 163 BNSS prohibitory orders are in force. It directed free movement in the city subject to law and order and traffic requirements, ordered the installation of barricades to be reviewed at once, and ordered prohibitory orders around the Supreme Court and other courts withdrawn. It also said lawyers, journalists and other professionals should not be hindered in discharging their professional duties.
Lawyers led by senior advocate Kapil Sibal told the court that police had continued detentions even in areas where prohibitory orders were not in force. Senior sdvocate Shadan Farasat, who was detained outside the Supreme Court on Saturday, said he was manhandled and bundled into a police vehicle. Senior advocate and Trinamool Congress MP Menaka Guruswamy called the episode an “undeclared emergency.”
CJP leader Ashutosh Ranka condemned the detention of journalists and remarked, “We are in a state of emergency.”
Contempt Plea Filed
A contempt petition was filed in the Supreme Court on October 12 by Free Speech Collective over the alleged detention and forcible removal of journalists. The plea alleged wilful disobedience of the Court’s October 11, 2026 order directing that lawyers, journalists and other professionals must not be hindered in discharging their professional duties. It sought contempt action, identification of the police officers and supervising officials responsible, and disclosure of how the order was communicated to personnel on the ground.
According to the plea, journalists continued to be detained and removed from reporting locations, including R K Ashram Marg and Connaught Place, despite identifying themselves as members of the press.

Elon Musk’s former partner Ashley St. Clair has alleged that the billionaire reduced her monthly child support payments after she publicly revealed the birth of their son, Romulus, in February 2025. Leh, Oct 18: Chief Justice of India Justice Surya Kant on Sunday said lawyers from Leh and Kargil would soon be able to virtually access the Supreme Court from the Ladakh Bench of the High Court.
All matters originating from Ladakh would be listed on a single day and heard through video-conferencing, sparing lawyers and litigants the time, cost and hardship of travelling to Delhi, Justice Kant said as he inaugurated the Ladakh Bench of the High Court of Jammu and Kashmir and Ladakh here.
Describing the inauguration as a historic step, the CJI referred to the establishment of a Special Court in Leh in 1870, observing that while the institution had passed into history, the geographical challenges that restricted access to justice persisted for generations.
"For close to a century, the high court that served Ladakh sat beyond the Great Himalayas, reachable in winter only by air," he said.
The CJI said the insertion of the name 'Ladakh' in a high court after it became a Union Territory in 2019 was an important step, but the gesture remained largely symbolic.
"A name on a court's letterhead is not the same as a court at one's doorstep," he said.
Justice Kant emphasised that the bench belongs equally to Leh and Kargil – the two districts in the Union Territory — and said its purpose would be served only when people in every corner of Ladakh start to feel a sense of ownership over the institution.
He also said that once video-conferencing facilities have been set up at the bench, the Supreme Court would list all matters originating from Ladakh on a single day and hear them on a day-to-day basis virtually.
The arrangement, the CJI said, would enable members of the Leh and Kargil bar associations to argue cases before the top court without leaving Ladakh.
"In this way, the distance will no longer stand between people of Ladakh and the highest Court of our country," he said.
Justice Kant said that the true measure of a court is not its geographical elevation but its accessibility to the people it serves.
"We are some 3,500 metres above the sea, and I am told no high court in our country has ever sat higher. Of course, what matters today is not how high this court sits. What is important is how close it now stands to the people it serves," he said.
The CJI recalled the role of village institutions and customary practices in resolving disputes, noting that the region had long relied on community-based mechanisms to uphold fairness and settle grievances.
On improving access to justice, he identified technology and legal aid as two essential instruments for overcoming geographical barriers.
"In a land of such vast distances, technology can do what no road ever could," he said. The CJI also underlined the importance of legal aid, calling it a constitutional promise that no citizen should be denied justice because of poverty or disability.
He stressed the need for legal awareness camps, para-legal volunteers, affordable legal representation, lok adalats and timely compensation for victims of crime.
"Access to justice, after all, begins not in the court's compound, but at the litigant's door," he said, expressing confidence that the Ladakh Legal Services Authority and the court's Legal Services Committee would work together to reach people awaiting justice in remote areas.
The CJI spoke of a young child studying in a classroom in Kargil or Nubra who might one day argue a case before the court or even serve as a judge on its bench.
"When that day comes, we will know that this bench has not merely arrived in Ladakh, but taken root here," Justice Kant said.

Aran Murphy is having quite a month, as he co-stars on not one, but two HBO shows — “Youth” and “War” — and plays one of the leads of Taika Waititi’s dystopian film “Klara and the Sun,” set to be released on Oct. 23. But if you think you’ve seen the 19-year-old actor before, it could be because of his strong resemblance to his Oscar-winning father, Cillian Murphy. “I don’t even think we look that much alike, but people seem to think otherwise,” the younger Murphy tells Variety.
In both “War” and “Youth,” Murphy plays a troubled teenager negotiating complex relationships with his parents as they navigate divorce. “Youth” follows Sharon Horgan as a rambunctious 50-year-old divorcée dipping back into the dating pool. As her son Rauri, Murphy plays a creepy, brooding university dropout whom audiences also can’t help sympathize with. After only a few days at school, he returns home because a rumor has been spread about him and a drunken hookup that suggests he may be a predator. Did Murphy decide for himself whether Rauri is to be believed about his innocence during the incident? “Yeah!” he says. “I mean, I’d like to think so. It’s up to the audience; I don’t decide that. But I want to back my character.”
Popular on Variety
Murphy’s and Rauri’s life trajectories are very different, but their timelines aren’t, which helped him get into character. “Contextually, we both just left school and were 18 — it was really about making decisions and whether college is the right thing, that kind of entrance into adult life, so that was a nice thing to draw on to relate to him,” he says.
He adds that Hogan’s strong scripts and professionalism helped Murphy find his footing on set.
“She was so awesome and charismatic and open to ideas that it was easy to just work and create that bond over shooting,” Murphy says. “The words were already so good, we were able to springboard off that and find the chemistry on the day.”
In “War,” Murphy has a raucous introduction in the Oct. 15 episode as Gabriel, who’s torn between his mother (Sienna Miller as Carla) and stepfather (Dominic West as Morgan) during their ugly, high-profile divorce. Caught between Carla, a past-her-prime actress, and Morgan, a billionaire social media entrepreneur, Gabriel finds himself in the crossfire, used as an asset to negotiate between them. Like Rauri in “Youth,” Murphy similarly credits his character’s duality and relatability to creator George Kay.
“It was all in the script — his frustration with what’s going on and nowhere to put it,” Murphy says. “I’m sure it’s a pretty universal kind of thing: People just want to take their anger out in some way.”
One manifestation of Gabriel’s anger is physical, meaning that Murphy needed to throw a punch while the character is drunk at a party after his friend makes a rude remark about his parents’ divorce.
“I’d never had to do something like that — that was new,” Murphy says. “That was a bit nerve-racking, because you don’t want to accidentally punch someone in the face.”
Acting professionally is all pretty new to Murphy. Despite growing up with artistic parents (his mother, Yvonne McGuinness, is an Irish visual artist), Murphy originally saw himself on the football field.
“That faded pretty quickly,” Murphy says. “I did a play when I was 11, and that was a really big deal for me. That was kind of the thing that showed me I wanted to [perform] for real when I became of age.”
Murphy, of course, grew up watching his father act. “Seeing my dad onscreen in dramatic situations as an 8-year-old was pretty full-on,” he says, mentioning Ken Loach war drama “The Wind That Shakes the Barley,” which won the Palme D’Or at the 2006 Cannes Film Festival. “I think I need to revisit it as a 19-year-old.”
He’s seen most, but “definitely not all,” of his father’s filmography, and is “forever grateful” for informing his film education at a young age, and having insightful conversations with him about acting. But Cillian’s biggest role for Murphy has been as a supportive father, rather than a public figure or acting influence. “I think living with someone who’s in the public eye, the novelty of that wears off pretty quick,” Murphy says.
Murphy was more starstruck by working with Waititi on “Klara and the Sun” starring Jenna Ortega and Amy Adams. Based on the novel by Kazuo Ishiguro, the film follows Ortega as a robot girl experiencing the grandeur of human life for the first time. Though the movie is coming out this month, it was shot in early 2024 when Murphy was 16.
“It was incredibly surreal. One minute I was in school, and then the next I was flying out to New Zealand and shooting a Taika Waititi film at 16, so it was just absolutely nuts,” Murphy says. “[Ortega and Adams] are so great, just being in their presence and being able to learn so much. They’re also so kind and accommodating. It’s just a massive learning experience, and I’m really grateful for it.”
Despite his pride in the project, he says he’s “not a fan” of AI, adding “I don’t think it’s a net positive for the industry.” For Murphy, this film is important for “opening those discussions” about AI and “talking about the importance of human life and especially friendship and love and human qualities.”
With this momentum behind him, Murphy says he’s eager to keep learning: “I’m just auditioning and crossing my fingers. Basically, I’m just open to anything.”

Delhi police have again obstructed protests in India’s capital as thousands of people returned to the streets, led by opposition leaders, to demand the resignation of the election commissioner.
After mass unrest in the capital over the weekend, when thousands were detained and harassed by police as they attempted to take part in a protest led by the gen Z Cockroach movement, on Monday the main opposition leaders led another procession through Delhi, this time to the supreme court.
The leader of India’s opposition alliance, Rahul Gandhi, alongside other opposition figures and student groups, had declared their intention to march to the court and submit a petition calling for India’s chief election commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar, to step down.
Kumar has become a deeply controversial figure for his role in an exercise to verify and “purify” India’s electoral rolls, which has led to more than 130m names – more than the population of Japan – being deleted from voter lists since last year.
Opposition parties and civil society groups allege Kumar implemented this special intensive revision (SIR) to help entrench the power of Narendra Modi’s government and his Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata party (BJP). Muslim voters and other minorities who are traditionally not BJP voters have allegedly been disproportionately affected by the deletions.
The election commission has denied favouring any party and said wrongly deleted voters could re-enrol, while the BJP has accused its rivals of trying to undermine democracy by questioning legitimate electoral processes.
Several metro stations were closed on Monday in central Delhi and police barricades prevented thousands of protesters getting within 600m of the supreme court, forcing them to turn back.
However, lawyers confirmed they had submitted the petition on Gandhi’s behalf and by late evening, Gandhi had broken through the barricades and reached the court gates.
In a press conference before the march, Gandhi reiterated his allegation that the Modi government was using the commission to commit “vote chori” (cheating) and accused Kumar of being a “thief”.
Gandhi expressed support for the mass uprising of young people, led by the Cockroach Janta party (CJP) and student groups, who had tried to protest over the weekend but were met with police brutality and mass detentions.
“Till the constitution is upheld, till the chief election commissioner is removed, till the system of elections is revamped, till justice is served for India, the youth won’t stop,” he said.
The SIR and calls for Kumar’s resignation have galvanised support for beleaguered opposition parties, who are seen to have flailed in the face of the BJP’s electoral power. Gandhi was detained twice last week after the police refused to let him and other opposition leaders reach Jantar Mantar, the designated protest site in central Delhi.
Mahua Moitra, an opposition MP who was marching after being detained last week, alleged that in her constituency in West Bengal more than 10,000 voters had been unjustly removed from the electoral rolls.
“There’s no going back now. People know that their votes have been stolen and this government is finished,” Moitra said. “The police can detain us, they can use brute force and crack our skulls, but we are not going to get off the streets until Gyanesh Kumar resigns and this government is gone. If we don’t stand up to this, then there will be nothing left of our country.”
Moitra accused the supreme court of helping to validate the SIR process and disenfranchise millions of Indians. “When the history of this dark chapter of India is written, the supreme court will be the most disgraced,” she said. “It was the supreme court who put a stamp of approval on every illegality of this government.”
Gandhi has spent months accusing the BJP of fraudulently influencing elections, but his claims have been largely ignored. The issue exploded last month after the Indian Express newspaper reported multiple irregularities in the SIR process that had been pushed through by Kumar.
The protests are likely to continue this week. On Monday, leaders of the CJP approached the Delhi police to seek a date to be allowed to hold a protest without obstruction. They said that if the police refused to comply, their supporters would take to the streets again.

Delhi court convicts man for shooting at wife outside hospital where she worked as security guard
New Delhi, A Delhi court has convicted a man for attempting to murder his wife by shooting her in the stomach outside a hospital in Connaught Place in 2018, saying the testimony of the injured woman was credible, trustworthy and sufficient to establish his guilt.
Additional Sessions Judge Dhirendra Rana, in a judgment dated October 13, held Sushant guilty under IPC Section 307 and Section 27 of the Arms Act, which deals with the use of arms.
The court, however, acquitted him of the charge under Section 25 of the Arms Act, which relates to illegal possession of a firearm.
It noted that a separate FIR for possession of the pistol was registered at Seelampur police station, and the trial in that case is pending before another court.
According to the prosecution, the incident took place on November 24, 2018, outside Gate No. 5 of Kalawati Hospital in Connaught Place. The victim, Pinki, worked as a security guard at the hospital and had been living at her parental home since her husband was sent to jail in a separate case in 2015.
Pinki told the court that Sushant, who had been released from jail about a month and a half earlier, came to the hospital in the evening and called her outside.
As she sat in an auto-rickshaw he had parked across the road, he asked whether she would return to her matrimonial home. When she refused, he fired a shot that hit her in the stomach and fled.
The victim said she was operated upon the same day, remained hospitalised for about a month, and underwent four surgeries in a short span.
The court said the evidence of the hospital staff, along with CCTV camera footage, established that the accused had come to the hospital and left with the victim shortly before she returned injured.
It noted that the owner of an auto-rickshaw testified that he had handed the vehicle to Sushant that day, and the vehicle was found abandoned near the spot with blood stains, and that later a forensic analysis matched the blood sample collected from the vehicle with the victim's DNA.
Citing several Supreme Court precedents, the court said the testimony of an injured witness carries great weight, as it comes with an inbuilt guarantee of presence at the scene, and that a conviction can rest on a single reliable witness.
The court said the defence failed to point to any reason why Pinki would falsely implicate her husband, beyond a "bald suggestion" of false implication arising from a matrimonial dispute.
"The accused fired upon the vital part of the body of the victim and, needless to say, he intended to eliminate the victim as she was not ready to live with the accused.
"Hence, the prosecution is successful in proving beyond reasonable doubt that the accused had attempted to commit murder of his wife Pinki and he stands convicted under Section 307 of the IPC," the judge said.
"I am of the considered view that the prosecution has successfully proved its case based on credible and trustworthy testimony of prosecution witness Pinki," he added.
The arguments on sentencing will be heard on a later date.

Flipkart-owned travel platform Cleartrip’s net loss widened 28.1% YoY to ₹805 Cr in FY26 from ₹628.4 Cr in FY25, as its expenses continued to outpace revenue growth. The online travel aggregator’s operating revenue grew 20.8% to ₹198.3 Cr during the year from ₹164.1 Cr in the previous fiscal. Including other income, Cleartrip reported total income of around ₹241.3 Cr, compared with ₹366.7 Cr in FY25. Other income declined 34.2% YoY to ₹43 Cr. Meanwhile, spending on cashbacks and discounts rose 47.5% to ₹897.5 Cr in FY26 from ₹608.2 Cr a year earlier, outpacing top line growth. Cleartrip generated ₹702.2 Cr from service charges and ₹378.4 Cr from commissions and incentives before accounting for cashbacks and discounts, taking the combined figure to around ₹1,095.7 Cr. These figures should be distinguished from the operating revenue reported in its financial statements. Founded in 2006 by Hrush Bhatt, Matthew Spacie and Stuart Crighton, Cleartrip enables users to book flights, hotels, trains, buses and local activities through its website and app. Ecommerce major Flipkart acquired the company in 2021. Cleartrip’s accumulated losses rose to ₹3,828 Cr as of March 31, 2026, from ₹3,023 Cr a year earlier. Its negative net worth also widened to ₹3,066 Cr from ₹2,262 Cr in FY25. In its financial statements, the company said its ability to continue as a going concern depended on the success of its operations and its ability to secure funding. However, it added that its holding company, Flipkart Internet Private Limited, had provided a commitment and letter of financial support. During FY26, Cleartrip borrowed ₹3,964 Cr from Flipkart Internet and repaid ₹3,653 Cr. Interest on these loans stood at ₹130.4 Cr for the year. The widening loss comes as Cleartrip seeks to reduce its reliance on discounts and diversify beyond flight bookings. In July 2026, the company said it was targeting operational break-even by the end of FY27. Its plans include growing its hotels, trains and buses businesses and increasing revenue from ancillary services. The company has also seen leadership changes in recent years. Anuj Rathi, who joined as CBO, stepped down in June 2025, less than a year after his appointment, to launch his venture, profound.me. He was succeeded by former Flipkart executive Manjari Singhal, who previously led the ecommerce company's beauty, FMCG and general merchandise businesses as vice-president and business head. Before Rathi's departure, long-standing CEO Ayyappan Rajagopal resigned from Cleartrip in August 2024 to launch quick-commerce startup FirstClub. Where Did Cleartrip Spend? Cleartrip’s total expenses increased 21.9% YoY to ₹1,045.9 Cr in FY26 from ₹858.2 Cr in FY25. Against operating revenue of ₹198.3 Cr, this translated into expenditure of ₹5.27 for every rupee earned from operations. Advertisement & Sales Promotion: Cleartrip’s spending on advertising and sales promotion rose 30.9% YoY to ₹133.8 Cr in FY26 from ₹102.2 Cr a year earlier. Employee Benefit Expenses: Employee costs increased 7.8% to ₹258.1 Cr from ₹239.4 Cr in FY25. Payment Gateway Charges: Payment processing expenses rose 40% YoY to ₹110.1 Cr from ₹78.7 Cr. Commission & Brokerage: Expenses under this head increased 33.2% YoY to ₹171.5 Cr from ₹128.8 Cr in FY25.

The NTPC is planning to initiate feasibility studies in a number of Indian states for proposed nuclear power projects as part of its drive to expand the generate of enegry from non-fossil-fuel sources to at least 2 GW by 2032, PTI reported citing a senior official. The NTPC, as part of its energy diversification strategy, is targeting to set up 30 GW of nuclear projects in the country to contribute to the government's ambitious 100 GW nuclear capacity target by 2047, as per PTI. A senior official told the news agency that studies in Madhya Pradesh, Bihar and Odisha have been carried out, and it will start looking for more locations in other states. Banka in Bihar, Basai in Madhya Pradesh and Nabarangpur in Odisha, the official said, adding, "More states will be explored as the vision is 30 GW nuclear capacity by 2047. Of course, Uttar Pradesh is on our list along with more states. We will conduct feasibility studies soon." He also revealed that the company's plan is to set up an average project having 1,400 MW with two units of 700 MW each. For a state government, the key question is whether it can offer a technically suitable, environmentally acceptable, and socially feasible site. Here are the key factors the NTPC will examine: The ready and uninterrupted supply of water is one of the biggest deciding factors, since conventional nuclear reactors need large, dependable water supplies for cooling as well as heat rejection. Thus, the sites need to be near perennial rivers or reservoirs, or have access to coaster seawater. It should also be ensured that water remains available during droughts and summer months. Competing requirements for drinking water, irrigation, and other industrial needs have to be ascertained. The NTPC has to look for a sufficiently large, contiguous site with clear ownership and which will also be able to accommodate the plant and its safety-related areas. Adequate land has to be available for reactor units, auxiliary facilities and cooling infrastructure. The population density around the site should be relatively low. The potential project should lead to limited displacement of villages, homes, or agricultural lands. The assessment will also consider the possible environmental impact of the project on forests, wildlife habitats, wetlands, groundwater, air and water quality. The ecologicsl effects of thermal discharges also need to be taken into account. Equipment like reactor vessels, steam generators, turbines and other heavy components require reliable routes for transportation. The NTPC will be examining the sites' access to railways, highways, ports where relevant, construction materials, skilled labour, accommodation and supporting industrial infrastructure. Sites in extremely remote locations can face higher construction costs and longer project schedules. A nuclear plant needs detailed examination of the ground beneath and around the proposed site. As per the Atomic Energy Regulatory Board (AERB) codal requirement, there should not be any active fault within 5 km radius from the proposed site of an NPP. These are some of the most important factors the NTPC will study to assess whether a site is suitable for a nuclear power plant. Some other factors include land and infrastructure costs, construction timelines, financing, grid connectivity and electricity demand, and others. Over the past week, the laptop Microsoft sent me has been summarizing books and movies, generating images from my imagination, and running a 70-billion-parameter AI model that would be a stretch to fit on most laptops. It also played AAA games at a speed and fidelity I would have thought impossible on an ARM system just a year ago. Microsoft wants to sell you one computer for all of your needs, and for once that doesn’t feel like total marketing fluff. Mostly.
Microsoft is throwing both arms around the new Nvidia RTX Spark platform with the Surface Laptop Ultra—and setting its sights on the would-be MacBook Pro buyer, or as the company called it, “a high performance audience.” The bet is that rather than a gaming desktop for fun and a development laptop for work, buyers will pay more for one machine that does both.
The Surface Laptop Ultra arrives at a strange time in personal computing. Recent industry numbers showed a 20 percent drop in total PC shipments year over year in the third quarter of 2026. That’s not just consumer purchasing either—that’s across the board. Between the RAMpocalypse that has exploded consumer prices and an industry fixated on enterprise money, there hasn’t been much new hardware to excite PC enthusiasts.
Microsoft isn’t the only one debuting an RTX-chipped laptop. Dell’s XPS 16 Creator Edition and Asus’s ProArt series (our own Ryan Whitwam‘s review should be appearing on the front page soon) are betting on the chipset as well. The question when reviewing the Surface Laptop Ultra isn’t whether it can achieve the things that it claims competently, but whether there’s finally a compelling reason for power users to switch to an ARM system, and whether their daily workloads can still be achieved without hiccups when compared to a more traditional x86 offering, or the biggest competitor within the segment, the MacBook Pro.
With a starting price of $2,599, this is not a budget alternative to Apple silicon. This is bleeding-edge hardware, and you’re going to be paying a premium for it. Depending on your selected processor and memory options, MSRP can reach as high as $5,899. Prospective buyers should note that the lower-specced 24GB unified memory model ships with Windows 11 Home, while the rest of the fleet arrives with Windows 11 Pro. I received the 64GB model for testing, and I think that would probably be the sweet spot for a lot of users to align cost and performance.
I really have to wonder if 24GB is enough to go around when we know that Windows 11 is memory-hungry on its own. When you have to assign a significant portion of that 24GB of unified memory to VRAM for gaming, does performance suffer? An audience question inside the Surface Laptop Ultra review information session asked about the usefulness of the base model, and didn’t get much back other than a vague “useful for smaller models locally” answer. Microsoft may have a more definitive answer to that question a few months from now when software and drivers catch up with hardware.
So has the Microsoft and Nvidia team-up created the ultimate all-in-one laptop? Or is this the industry once again putting the hardware hype cart before the finished-software horse?

Display
The 15-inch mini-LED display might not be enough to get folks to run to the Ultra on its own, but it’s a compelling reason to add it to the list. The 3270×2180 native resolution looks simply stunning whether you’re watching a 4K video, playing games, or just staring at a desktop spreadsheet. I preferred the Enhanced color profile, but Vivid and sRGB modes looked fantastic as well.
Blacks stayed deep against bright, vivid subjects without any sort of visible blooming. I wish I could say the same for my TV. While I can’t quantify how it stacks side by side with the latest MacBook Pro Retina display, I can say that this is a damn nice screen. Viewing angles are superb, colors are punchy, and the 2,000-nit peak brightness kept things legible even in a room flooded with natural sunlight. My only gripe is that in bright rooms, there is glare to contend with. The glossy glass looks fantastic at lower light levels but can act a bit mirror-like in direct sunlight. It hindered my ability to photograph the screen more than it did my ability to use the computer. Still, if you’re looking for a matte-screen laptop, you might want to keep that in mind.
Keyboard and trackpad
The keyboard on the Surface Laptop Ultra is exactly what you’d expect on a premium machine like this. It’s excellent, if unremarkable. The keys have a shallow but satisfying press, the spacing makes sense for my hands, and the whole package delivers a very comfortable typing experience. I don’t have a whole bunch of laptops lying around to compare it to, but unsurprisingly, the closest would be my 2020 MacBook Pro. Microsoft knows what market it’s going after here, and I don’t mind them lifting direct inspiration from Apple in this department.
The trackpad is similarly competent. It’s absolutely huge, measuring 5.5 inches long by 3.5 inches tall, with excellent tracking accuracy throughout my testing time. Normally, one of the first things I do when plugging in a laptop to work from is to attach an external mouse, but over days of testing, I never reached for the mouse drawer. Microsoft made a point to emphasize the trackpad’s haptic feedback capabilities in native programs during the review information session. I’m not sure if there are still updates left to come that I haven’t received yet, but I can’t recall a time when I noticed additional mouse haptics had kicked in when I opened MS Office or anything. As it stands, the trackpad isn’t groundbreaking, but it is premium enough to be part of an “ultra” laptop.
Magnetic USB-C charging
Microsoft describes the included magnetic charging connection and port as being “the world’s first built-in magnetic USB-C charging experience.” It’s difficult to get upset about the marketing department doing their jobs, but this claim struck me as more of a technical truth than engineering feat. Apple’s MagSafe charging debuted on the original MacBook Pro all the way back in 2006. The concept of a breakaway magnetic charger isn’t anything new, but technically Microsoft’s assertion holds water in that it is the first USB-C connector on a laptop with a matching magnetic port, rather than a proprietary connector.
Marketing claims aside, the magnetic connection does work well. The port and charger naturally guide themselves together, as magnets do, and made plugging the laptop in to charge in a dark room hassle-free. Normally I’d be holding the cord in one hand while trying to fumble around in the dark for the phone in my pocket and remember the gesture to quickly turn on the flashlight. Now I just have to get the cable within the vicinity, and the magnets do the rest. Perfect for when all I want to do is plug the PC in and go to bed.
What’s perhaps the larger selling point for magnetic charging is the cable’s ability to break away if yanked from the PC. Nothing will ruin your day faster than watching a new laptop fly off the counter. With the breakaway cable, you’re getting peace of mind that your laptop shouldn’t meet the floor should a startled cat or curious toddler come into contact with the cable. I’ve never had it happen with one of my laptops, but that doesn’t mean accidents don’t occur. I simulated a few ‘accidental disconnects’ with modest force, and the cable disconnected dutifully as it should.
While I won’t say that it’s a must-have, it’s certainly a nice-to-have. And in this package it’s certainly the type of premium accessory you’d expect, but it’s not going to move units on its own—not at these price tiers.
Geekbench
According to Nvidia, the RTX Spark N1X is a Grace CPU fused to a Blackwell GPU. Unlike chipsets like AMD’s Ryzen AI and Intel’s Core Ultra series, the N1X has no dedicated NPU—instead it leans on unified memory and the heavy-duty Blackwell GPU for AI work. Traditionally, Copilot+ certification has hinged on a 40+ TOPS NPU, but Microsoft is extending the label to this machine’s GPU-based AI performance anyway (more on that later).
The graphics bench tests sing when given access to 40GB+ of usable RAM. These results certainly back up Microsoft’s claims that the Surface Laptop Ultra can handle modern AAA gaming. It just takes some different paths to performance than we might be used to.
The AI benchmark was a bit of a miss. I don’t have the ability to run an NPU-accelerated benchmark in Geekbench AI, because the software presumably doesn’t currently have a compatible NPU backend for this unique architecture. Curiously, Windows does list a generic NPU under Display Adapters in Device Manager, but Geekbench AI only offered the ONNX CPU testing path. It’s unclear whether the generic NPU listed by Windows is a virtual device, some sort of driver exposure, or something else entirely.
It isn’t possible to get performance metrics on hardware that Geekbench can’t properly see yet. It’s still early days, but it’s the kind of software/hardware incompatibility that you hate to run into when just trying to check out what your new computer can do. The CPU score in Geekbench AI isn’t particularly impressive, and bypassing the Blackwell sort of defeats the purpose of this hardware, so I hope that as the RTX Spark devices start getting out there, we’ll be able to get a better idea of the full potential.

AI testing (where possible) with AI Dev Gallery
Microsoft recommended reviewers try its new AI Dev Gallery app (preview) as a way to test on-device AI. The software is currently in public preview, and users can pull models of their choice directly from Hugging Face for testing or workflow. The project’s GitHub carries a helpful word of warning about running models on ARM64-based Copilot+ PCs, which, according to Microsoft, this is. Or will be, eventually. Confusing, isn’t it?
⚠️ Note: On ARM64-based Copilot+ PCs, make sure to build and run the solution as ARM64 (and not as x64). This is required, especially when running the samples that communicate with models such as Phi Silica.
On paper, AI Dev Gallery should have been a simple one-stop shop to test a barrage of different models against the Surface Laptop Ultra’s new RTX Spark setup. In practice, all of the available conversational Phi and Mistral models in the app are CPU-only—no GPU or NPU pathways available, despite the Blackwell sitting there idling. GPU and NPU paths are available for some image generation and embedded model options, but it again leaves me with that lingering feeling that we’re pushing cutting edge hardware just to have something to offer the market. Oh, and it’s worth noting that twice during my testing, I was browsing AI Dev Gallery’s model selection when the program abruptly froze and then crashed entirely back to desktop. There are still rough edges to smooth out.
Phi Silica, Microsoft’s flagship on-device LLM and a major piece of the Copilot+ stack, cannot be accessed out of the gate. Accessing the API requires a developer registration with an associated app identity. These may seem like obvious steps for those already in the AI-know, but curious consumers might get frustrated by reaching a gate in what is advertised as a ready-to-run experience out of the box.
AI Dev Gallery conversational model (Mistral 7B Instruct 0.2 CPU) — Cutting out the GPU, this CPU-only model was still able to manage about 11 tokens/sec. Slower than a GPU path for sure, but it’s interesting that the CPU alone can manage smaller models at a reasonable conversation rate.
AI Dev Gallery image generation(Stable Diffusion v1.4) — I attempted image generation harnessing the CPU by accident at first. That didn’t fare so well, but as soon as I switched over to the NvTensorRT (GPU) option, I was able to generate images from a prompt in about three to four seconds by my stopwatch. The results aren’t the best you’ve ever seen, but with additional prompting and image coaxing, I’m confident that they could have been improved. Whether you need local AI image generation on your daily driver is another matter.
I attempted to follow Microsoft’s instructions listed in the AI Dev Gallery to run a CUDA-accelerated Phi model, but the process failed. After resolving some command-line issues, pip downloaded the correct Python 3.13 package of onnxruntime-genai-cuda for Windows ARM64, but then failed because the required onnxruntime-gpu dependency doesn’t seem to have a compatible distribution for this environment. Logs indicated the CUDA install path wasn’t usable on this setup at this time. Whether this is a limitation of the current package, an ARM64 packaging gap, or human error, I can’t be totally sure. It was just frustrating to feel so limited in the space where Microsoft told me to play.

Ollama
Frustrated with the current state of Microsoft’s AI Dev Gallery app, I decided to try some testing via Ollama running locally in the command prompt. I downloaded the Llama3.3-70b model. That’s a 43GB model—10 times the size of the Mistral model we ran on the CPU in AI Dev Gallery, with 10 times the parameters (70 billion over 7).
If I were Microsoft, this is the type of demo I’d want to be showing off. This massive 70B model would be unlikely to run on any discrete laptop GPU, but the Blackwell still managed 6.26 tokens/sec. The fact that it ran at all is impressive, though I will say this was one of the few times when the Blackwell really seemed to be sweating. System fans were spinning at 100 percent while those Wayne’s World synopses were being written. Credit where due, even at full tilt, the fans don’t generate a lot of sound other than the high-speed pushing of air.

Gaming
When Microsoft speaks of a high performance audience, none is more demanding than the modern high-end PC gamer. I’m old enough that I still find 1080p/60 Hz gaming to look great, and that’s probably for the best, given the current cost of video cards, but those who crave the zero input lag, 4K, ray-traced life are a particular bunch. Whether the package on offer with the Surface Laptop Ultra will be high performance enough for that audience will be up to the individual gamer and their wallet, but this gamer was certainly impressed that these results were coming out of an ARM machine.
Microsoft claims 85 percent of its Game Pass library is currently playable on ARM, but I had difficulty trying to find if any titles have a native ARM port, or if they were running in x64 through the Prism lens of emulation. Windows Performance Fit offers a glimpse into how the game might perform on your system, but nothing more. Either way, if it’s the playing of games that you’re concerned with, there shouldn’t be much this system won’t run. The full Nvidia DLSS feature set seems to be available, and ray tracing boxes can be clicked in graphics options. Factor in an HDR-capable display, and the Surface Laptop Ultra is covering a lot of the must-haves for modern gamers.
After an initial boot of Gears of War: E-Day that saw a solid 4–5 minutes of shader compiling, I was concerned that this might be an every-time occurrence, but subsequent loads were much faster. This is a game that contains anti-cheat, the latest Unreal Engine, and all the imaginable graphical bells and whistles you’d want from one of your company’s prized franchises. It’s here and running quite well on the Surface Laptop Ultra. While benchmarking, I noticed the system had reported an astonishing 46.7GiB of its 64GiB of unified memory as available VRAM for the game.
To their credit, Microsoft has included a warning for consumers who might not be familiar with the new Surface Laptop Ultra architecture: “App compatibility: Surface Laptop Ultra runs Windows 11 on an Arm-based Nvidia RTX Spark platform. Many popular apps run natively on Arm. Apps that are not built for Arm can run through Prism, Windows’ built-in emulator. If you rely on specialized hardware drivers, plug-ins, or older utilities, check app and driver compatibility before purchase.”
Multiplayer titles with kernel-level anti-cheat measures may fail or show warnings under Prism emulation due to signature mismatches in system files. Each time I ran Gears of War: E-Day, I was greeted with a warning message when exiting back into Windows. It appears as though the Easy Anti-Cheat was flagging the .NET cache as “modified,” though I couldn’t establish whether Prism’s translation was directly responsible.

HandBrake
Beyond gaming, I wanted to see how video encoding would fare on the new hardware. I ran a real-world encode test via HandBrake on the 2160p 60 fps version of the famous Big Buck Bunny. The system processed the 10-minute video clip in 2:27 at 180 fps using x264 encoding via the CPU. That’s the snag. Nvidia NVENC or Nvidia HEVC encoding options are nowhere to be found, meaning the Blackwell’s encode engine still isn’t being exposed to the software. That’s not a problem with HandBrake, it’s just the continuation of a familiar pattern. Hardware decode worked just fine via Media Foundation, so it’s specifically the encode side of things running into a roadblock.
Copilot+
According to Microsoft in the review information session I attended, the Surface Laptop Ultra will be certified as a Copilot+ device, but “full software support won’t arrive until late 2026 or early 2027.” The keyboard’s dedicated Copilot button launches the window for M365 Copilot right now, which is fine if you intended to use it for Cloud AI services, but users may be confused at first given the package they were sold.
Features like Recall, Click to Do, and the new Windows search bar won’t be available until Microsoft finishes baking them for the Surface Laptop Ultra’s hardware. Participants in the Windows Insider Program will likely see early access before the general public, so if you’re itching for those Copilot+ features, you’ll have to agree to participate and share device information with Microsoft. Your call.
Unscientific battery testing
Since the Surface Laptop Ultra is meant to be an all-day device that can handle your workload during the day and your gaming at night, there’s an unavoidable question of how much of that you can actually do on the go. With this in mind, I attempted to measure battery levels every 30 minutes throughout my testing and mapped it to a partial day of mixed use.
